definition_zh: 巧妙移动；机动动作；军事演习；[美式] 施计策；操纵；巧妙的策略
definition_en: a skillful movement or planned action, especially one involving large vehicles or troops, or to move or act in such a skillful way
core_image: 手不停操作：驾驶员双手快速转动方向盘，让庞然大物躲开障碍
scene: 暴雨后的山路上，货车司机不急不躁地转动方向盘，绕过了塌下来的碎石。The driver began to maneuver the truck around the rocks and fallen trees.
sceneCN: 这里 maneuver 是「（熟练地）移动、操控」（第 1 个义项：用技巧让庞然大物在人缝里走位）；句意：司机开始操控卡车绕过落石与倒树。图中可辨识物件：盘山公路、货车、碎石坡、方向盘。

pos.zh: 巧妙的移动；计谋；策略；军事演习
巧妙移动；灵活走位；施计策

collocations.zh: 把车巧妙地挪进（车位等）

derivatives.zh: 由 maneuver 加 -able 构成，义为「机动灵活的、易于操控的」
maneuverable 加 -ity 构成，义为「机动性；操控性」
maneuver 加 -ing 构成的名词，义为「腾挪；周旋的动作」
英式拼写的同义形容词，义为「易于操控的」

senses.title: A careful physical movement
senses.definition: a movement made carefully and skillfully, especially to avoid something or get into a tight place
senses.definitionCN: 小心而有技巧地做出的一次移动，尤指为了避开某物或挪进狭窄位置
senses.example: It took three tries to maneuver the sofa through the doorway.
senses.exampleCN: 把沙发挪过门口试了三次才成功。
senses.why: The word started in French as handiwork; putting a big or awkward object where it belongs is still conceived as skilled work done with the hands.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在法语里本是「手工劳作」；把笨重物件挪到该去的地方，至今仍被看作一种双手操作的技巧活，所以最具体的一义就是「熟练腾挪」。

senses.title: A planned military or naval exercise
senses.definition: a planned movement of troops, ships, or aircraft, especially as a training operation
senses.definitionCN: 军队、舰船或飞机的有计划的调动，尤指作为训练而进行
senses.example: The fleet held large-scale maneuvers in the open sea.
senses.exampleCN: 舰队在公海上进行了大规模演习。
senses.why: An army is the largest awkward object of all, so the same hand-like handling of bodies moved into soldiers, ships and aircraft.
senses.whyCN: 军队是最大也最笨重的「物件」，于是这种像用手搬动东西一样的操作，自然延伸到部队、舰船与飞机的调动和演习。

senses.title: A clever scheme or trick
senses.definition: a clever or sometimes dishonest plan used to gain an advantage
senses.definitionCN: 为取得优势而使用的巧妙、有时并不诚实的计划
senses.example: His last-minute resignation was a clever maneuver to avoid questions.
senses.exampleCN: 他在最后一刻辞职，是躲开追问的巧妙手腕。
senses.why: Moving an object cleverly became moving people and situations cleverly, so any contrived plan earns the name.
senses.whyCN: 巧妙移动物件变成了巧妙调动人和局势，于是任何精心设计的计划都被称作 maneuver，这一义带点「耍手段」的意味。

senses.title: To move skillfully around obstacles
senses.definition: to move a vehicle or oneself with skill, especially through a narrow or crowded place
senses.definitionCN: 技巧性地移动车辆或本人，尤指穿过狭窄或拥挤的地方
senses.example: She maneuvered her bicycle between the parked cars.
senses.exampleCN: 她骑着自行车在停放的汽车之间灵巧穿行。
senses.why: As a verb the word keeps the hands in charge, so the movement is always aimed at a gap or around an obstacle.
senses.whyCN: 作动词时「手在操作」的画面仍在，所以动作总朝着空隙而去、绕开障碍而行，强调技巧而非力气。

senses.title: To move a person into a position
senses.titleCN: 设法使……进入（某位置或处境）
senses.definition: to move or guide a person into a particular place or situation through careful steps
senses.definitionCN: 通过细致的步骤把人移到某个位置或处境
senses.example: The host maneuvered me toward the empty seat at the far end.
senses.exampleCN: 主人设法把我引向尽头的空座位。
senses.why: Hands that place objects can also place people, so the verb describes guiding someone gently but deliberately.
senses.whyCN: 摆物的手也能摆人，于是动词可指温和却刻意地把某人引到某个位置，中心意义就是那句朴素的英文「把人挪到某处」。

senses.title: To scheme for advantage
senses.definition: to act in a clever and often unfair way in order to gain something
senses.definitionCN: 为取得某物而巧妙、常常并不公平地行动
senses.example: Both sides maneuvered for control of the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 双方为控制委员会各施手腕。
senses.why: Once the word names scheming, the verb can describe the scheming itself, and gains a slightly critical tone.
senses.whyCN: 一旦名词义项长出了「计谋」，动词也就带上施计的色彩，语意略含批评，常出现在政治、商业与竞选的语境。

senses.title: Room to act freely
senses.definition: the freedom or space to change plans or act differently
senses.definitionCN: 改变计划或另作安排的自由与空间
senses.example: The new rules leave little room for maneuver.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定几乎没有留下回旋余地。
senses.why: If a vehicle needs space in which to steer, freedom of action can be measured in the same way, giving the common phrase about room to act.
senses.whyCN: 既然车辆转弯需要空间，行动的自由也能用空间来度量，于是「是否还有挪动的余地」成了评价政策与谈判的常用说法。

intro.en: Maneuver comes from French manoeuvre, from Latin manu operari, to work with the hand.
intro.cn: maneuver 来自法语 manoeuvre，源头是拉丁语 manu operari，意为「用手劳作」。

items.en: Manus means hand, and operari means to work.
items.cn: manus 意为手，operari 意为劳作。

items.en: Manuoperari describes the work a hand does.
items.cn: manuoperari 描述手上的劳作。

items.en: Manouvrer means to work with the hands and later to manage.
items.cn: manouvrer 意为用手劳作，后来也指操持、打理事务。

items.en: Maneuver enters English as a term for army movements.
items.cn: maneuver 进入英语，最初指军队的调动。

items.en: The word spreads to vehicles, clever plans and free room to act.
items.cn: 词义扩展到交通工具、巧妙的计谋与行动的自由空间。

note.en: Maneuver belongs to the hand-work family of manu- and to the everyday vocabulary of steering and scheming.
note.cn: maneuver 属于 manu-（手）词族，也落在「驾驶、走位、耍手腕」这组日用词汇里。

entries.definitionCN: maneuver 的英式拼写，读音相同

entries.definition: to handle or control something skillfully, often unfairly
entries.definitionCN: 巧妙处理或操控，常含不义之意；同源于「手」的词根

entries.definition: done with or using the hands
entries.definitionCN: 用手完成的；同源于拉丁语 manus（手）

entries.definition: to control the direction of a vehicle

normalIntro.en: Maneuver remembers the hand: manu- is Latin for hand, and the word still means moving things as if by careful hand.
normalIntro.cn: maneuver 记住「手」：拉丁语 manu- 即手，这个词至今指像用手一样细细搬弄。

normal.en: Manu- means hand, as in manual and manipulate.
normal.cn: manu- 表示手，manual 与 manipulate 都含这个词根。

normal.en: Manuoperari is Latin for working with the hands.
normal.cn: manuoperari 这个拉丁短语意为用手劳作。

normal.en: Maneuver a car means steering it with skill.
normal.cn: maneuver a car 指熟练地驾驶汽车。

normal.en: Military maneuvers are practice movements of troops.
normal.cn: military maneuvers 指部队的演练调动。

normal.en: Room for maneuver means freedom to change course.
normal.cn: room for maneuver 指改变路线的余地。

abstract.en: Picture two hands turning a wide ship inch by inch.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手一寸寸地转动一艘巨轮。

abstract.en: See toy soldiers being laid out on a table before a quiet match.
abstract.cn: 想象一桌小兵在无声的比试前被一一摆好阵位。

abstract.en: Think of a chess player moving a piece while smiling at you.
abstract.cn: 想象一位棋手一边挪动棋子，一边对你微笑。

examples.en: Careful maneuvering got the boat into the narrow harbour.
examples.cn: 小心翼翼地操控，才把船驶进了狭窄的港湾。

examples.en: The soldiers practiced maneuvers in the hills near the border.
examples.cn: 士兵们在边境附近的山地进行了演习。

examples.en: Some delegates saw the delay as a political maneuver.
examples.cn: 一些代表把这次拖延看作政治手腕。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马挪」——马挪开身子让路，就是 maneuver 的避让走位；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关（真正词源见「手」）。

root: 拉丁语 manus（手）+ operari（劳作）→ 中世纪拉丁语 manuoperari（用手操作）→ 古法语 manouvrer（劳作、操持）→ 英语 maneuver，核心义「用手般的技巧去摆布」。

sensesIntro.en: Maneuver begins with skilled hand-like movement, extends to troop movements and to clever plans, and finally becomes the very freedom to act.
sensesIntro.cn: maneuver 先指像手操作一样的有技巧的移动，再延伸到部队调动与巧妙的计谋，最后抽象成行动的自由。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands carefully turning and placing something large.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手小心地转动、摆放一件庞然大物。

branches.en: A careful, skillful movement of an object is the concrete sense.
branches.cn: 对物件的一次有技巧的移动是最具体的义项。

branches.en: Troops and ships are moved as one great object.
branches.cn: 部队与舰船被当作一件巨大的物件来移动，即军事演习。

branches.en: Scheming is the same cleverness turned on people, as noun and verb.
branches.cn: 耍手腕是把同一份巧劲用在人身上，名词与动词各有一面。

branches.en: The verb keeps the hands in charge, moving cars or guiding a person.
branches.cn: 动词义仍是手在操作：或驾着车穿行，或把人引到某处。

branches.en: Room for maneuver turns the physical space into freedom of action.
branches.cn: 回旋余地把物理上的空间抽象成行动的自由。

intro.en: Maneuver is the hand-work word: man- from manus carries the hand, and operari carries the labour.
intro.cn: maneuver 是「手上的活」：man- 来自 manus（手），operari 带来「劳作」之义。

latinIntro.en: Latin manus means hand and operari means to work, and their joining gives the French word behind maneuver.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 manus 意为手，operari 意为劳作，二者结合构成了英语词背后的法语形式。

items.example: The root manu- appears in all hand-related words.
items.exampleCN: 词根 manu- 出现在所有与手有关的词里。

items.example: Manus is the source of the hand image.
items.exampleCN: manus 提供了「手」的画面。

items.example: Operari gives the labour part of the word.
items.exampleCN: operari 带来「劳作」那一部分。

items.example: Manouvrer is the direct French form.
items.exampleCN: manouvrer 是直接来源的法语形式。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或结果的词尾
items.example: The ending -ure turns the verb into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ure 把动词变成名词。

items.example: The suffix -able forms maneuverable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 maneuverable。

items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 maneuverability。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms the noun maneuvering.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成名词 maneuvering。

items.example: Maneuverable describes a small boat.
items.exampleCN: maneuverable 用来形容小船灵活。

latinEntries.meaning: a handful, a body of troops

definition_zh: 狂热；一时风行的热潮；癖好；精神病学中的躁狂；〔构词后缀〕……癖；……狂
definition_en: a strong, often temporary enthusiasm for something, a craze, or in psychiatry a state of abnormally high mood and energy
core_image: 一圈人围住橱窗里的小玩偶，眼睛发亮，谁也停不下来
scene: 街头小店里，人们为了抢购某一款玩具排起长队，谁劝都不走。Collectors around the world joined the mania for the little toys.
sceneCN: 这里 mania 是「狂热；一时风行的热潮」（第 1 个义项：很多人对某物同时着迷的风潮）；句意：世界各地的收藏者都加入了这场小玩偶的热潮。图中可辨识物件：玩具橱窗、排队的人群、闪亮的眼睛。

derivatives.zh: man- + -iac 构成，义为「疯子；狂热者」，口语引申为「对某事上瘾的人」
从 mania 截短加 -ic 构成，义为「躁狂的；狂热的」
借 mania 的第一个成分 man-（手）另造，指「修指甲」，并非表示狂热的派生词
mono-（单一）+ mania 构成，义为「偏执于一件事」
megalo-（巨大）+ mania 构成，义为「夸大狂；自大狂」

senses.title: A craze for something
senses.definition: a very strong interest in or enthusiasm for something that spreads among many people
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物非常强烈的兴趣或热情，并在很多人之间蔓延
senses.example: The skateboard mania spread from town to town.
senses.exampleCN: 滑板热潮从一个城镇蔓延到另一个城镇。
senses.why: The Greek noun mania described madness, and a crowd that loses its head over a new toy moves like one possessed person multiplied, so a feverish craze keeps the name.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 mania 本指「疯癫」；一群人为了新玩具而失去理智，就像一个疯子被复制了无数份，所以这种发烧般的热潮沿用同一个词。

senses.title: An obsessive personal habit
senses.definition: a strong and often unreasonable desire or habit that belongs to one person
senses.definitionCN: 属于某个人、强烈而常不合理的欲望或习惯
senses.example: He has a mania for tidying other people desks.
senses.exampleCN: 他有个怪癖，喜欢整理别人的书桌。
senses.why: When the madness lives inside a single person, the word names a ruling habit or a fixed idea rather than a public fashion.
senses.whyCN: 当这种「疯劲」只活在一个人身上时，词义就从公共时尚收窄为个人的支配性习惯或执念。

senses.title: A psychiatric state
senses.definition: a mental state of abnormally raised mood, energy, speech, and behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 情绪、精力、言谈与行为异常高涨的精神状态
senses.example: The doctor explained that mania is not the same as simple happiness.
senses.exampleCN: 医生解释说，躁狂并不等同于单纯的快乐。
senses.why: The medical use returns to the oldest sense, the loss of control of the mind, while adding clinical precision about mood and energy.
senses.whyCN: 医学用法回到了最古老的一层「心智失控」，同时补上了对情绪与精力的临床界定，使这个词可以当诊断术语使用。

senses.title: An epidemic of frenzy in history
senses.definition: a mass outburst of wild shared behaviour described in historical and medical accounts
senses.definitionCN: 历史与医学记述中一群人同时发生的癫狂行为
senses.example: Records describe a dancing mania that lasted for days in one town.
senses.exampleCN: 一些记载描述了一个镇上持续数日的跳舞狂潮。
senses.why: A whole crowd repeating one wild act shows how deeply the madness sense survives whenever mania crosses from one mind into many.
senses.whyCN: 整整一群人重复同一个狂乱动作，说明「疯」这一层始终潜伏在词里，只要它从一个脑袋扩散到许多脑袋，就成了历史上的集体癫狂。

senses.title: As a combining form
senses.definition: a suffix meaning an extreme and often unhealthy interest in the thing named before it
senses.definitionCN: 作后缀，表示对前面所述之物极端且常不健康的兴趣
senses.example: Critics have called the film a symptom of buying mania.
senses.exampleCN: 影评人把这部电影称作购买癖的表征。
senses.why: Because mania is a state one can fall into, it attaches easily to the object of the obsession and lives on as a productive ending.
senses.whyCN: 因为 mania 是一种能「陷进」的状态，它很容易挂到痴迷对象的后面，从而变成能产的后缀式成分。

intro.en: Mania comes from Greek mania, madness, related to mainesthai, to be mad, often without a settled deeper origin.
intro.cn: mania 来自希腊语 mania（疯癫），与动词 mainesthai（发疯）相关，更深的来源一般认为尚不确定。

items.en: Manie means madness or frenzy, and mania is its noun.
items.cn: 希腊语 manie 意为疯、狂，mania 是与之同根的名词。

items.en: Mainesthai means to be mad or inspired.
items.cn: mainesthai 意为发疯或进入迷狂。

items.en: Hippocratic writers use mania for one of the main forms of mental illness.
items.cn: 希波克拉底医学文献把 mania 用作主要精神病症之一的名称。

items.en: Mania is carried into the Latin medical vocabulary.
items.cn: mania 被带入拉丁语的医学词汇。

items.en: Mania enters English as a medical term for mental disorder.
items.cn: mania 进入英语，最初是表示精神疾患的医学用语。

items.en: In the twentieth century it widens to any popular craze.
items.cn: 到了二十世纪，词义扩展到任何流行的热潮。

note.en: Mania sits between the Greek madness family and the everyday words for fashions and obsessions.
note.cn: mania 处在希腊语「疯狂」词族与日常「时尚、痴迷」词汇的交界处。

entries.definition: relating to mania, or extremely energetic
entries.definitionCN: 躁狂的；极度亢奋的，由 mania 变形而来

entries.definition: a person in a state of violent madness or extreme enthusiasm
entries.definitionCN: 疯子；狂热分子，同一词源的人名词

entries.definition: cosmetic care of the hands and nails
entries.definitionCN: 修指甲；只借了 man-（手）造词，与狂热义无关

entries.definition: a short-lived but intense popular fashion
entries.definitionCN: 一时的狂热；时尚

entries.definition: a thought or interest that dominates the mind
entries.definitionCN: 痴迷；执念

entries.definition: a feeling of extreme happiness, sometimes abnormal
entries.definitionCN: 极度兴奋；（医学上）欣快感

normalIntro.en: Mania keeps two lives in one word: a clinical madness and a joyful crowd craze.
normalIntro.cn: mania 在一个词里保有两条命：一种是临床上的「狂」，一种是众人雀跃的「热」。

normal.en: A mania for something means an uncontrollable enthusiasm.
normal.cn: a mania for 某事物指对它的狂热。

normal.en: The suffix -manic builds words such as kleptomania.
normal.cn: 后缀式 -manic 能构成 kleptomania 这类词。

normal.en: Manic is the adjective and maniac the person.
normal.cn: manic 是形容词，maniac 是那个人。

normal.en: Dancing mania names a famous mass frenzy of the Middle Ages.
normal.cn: dancing mania 指中世纪一场著名的集体癫狂。

normal.en: Compare craze: a mania may be harmful, a craze simply fashionable.
normal.cn: 对比 craze：mania 可能有害，craze 只是赶时髦。

abstract.en: Picture a tight circle of shoppers pressing against a shop window.
abstract.cn: 想象一群顾客紧紧围住商店橱窗往里挤。

abstract.en: See one office worker who cannot leave a crooked frame alone.
abstract.cn: 想象一个职员见不得歪掉的画框，非要把它摆正。

abstract.en: Imagine a sleepless patient pacing the ward all night at full speed.
abstract.cn: 想象一位失眠的病人整夜在病房里快步来回。

examples.en: The mania for online shopping grew during the sales season.
examples.cn: 网购狂热在促销季愈演愈烈。

examples.en: Her mania for neatness made sharing a desk difficult.
examples.cn: 她爱整洁到近乎癖好，与人共用书桌很不容易。

examples.en: The dancing mania of medieval Europe remains a mystery.
examples.cn: 中欧中世纪的跳舞狂潮至今仍是个谜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「买你呀」——看见什么都想「买你呀」，正是种停不下来的狂热；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 mania（疯癫、迷狂），与 mainesthai（发疯）同源，更早的原始印欧语来源一般认为不确定；经拉丁语医学词汇进入英语，核心义「心智被某种东西攫住」。

sensesIntro.en: Mania starts as madness, then splits into a private obsession, a clinical state, a mass frenzy, and finally a suffix for any ruling passion.
sensesIntro.cn: mania 从「疯」出发，分岔为个人的执念、临床的躁狂、群体的癫狂，最后沉淀成表示「癖好」的构词成分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ring of bright-eyed people pressed against a shop window.
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈眼睛发亮的人紧紧贴着商店橱窗。

branches.en: A shared craze is the madness sense spread out into a crowd.
branches.cn: 共同的热潮，是把「疯」这一层扩散到人群之中。

branches.en: A private obsession is the same force confined to one person.
branches.cn: 个人的癖好，是同一股力量被关在一个人身上。

branches.en: Clinical mania and historical mass frenzy keep the oldest medical sense.
branches.cn: 临床躁狂与历史集体癫狂保留了最古老的医学含义。

branches.en: Popular enthusiasm becomes a suffix attached to its favourite object.
branches.cn: 流行热情最终变成后缀，挂到痴迷对象的名字后面。

branches.en: Both a habit and an illness describe a mind that cannot let go.
branches.cn: 癖好与病症都描述一颗放不下、停不下来的心。

intro.en: Mania is a Greek root word that also works as a productive ending, as in kleptomania and megalomania.
intro.cn: mania 既是希腊语词根，也能当能产后缀使用，如 kleptomania 与 megalomania。

latinIntro.en: The Greek noun mania passed into Latin medical writing as mania, and from there into English.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语名词 mania 进入拉丁医学文献时拼作 mania，再由英语借用。

items.example: Mania is the Greek source of the word.
items.exampleCN: mania 是这个词的希腊语来源。

items.example: Mainesthai is the related verb of madness.
items.exampleCN: mainesthai 是表示发疯的相关动词。

items.exampleCN: 词尾 -manic 出现在 manic 与 monomanic 中。

items.example: The prefix mono- gives monomania.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 mono- 构成 monomania。

items.example: The prefix megalo- gives megalomania.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 megalo- 构成 megalomania。

items.example: The prefix klepto- gives kleptomania.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 klepto- 构成 kleptomania。

definition_zh: 明显的；显露；显现；证明；〔清单〕载货单；乘客名单
definition_en: easy to see or understand; to show something clearly; or an official list of goods or passengers
core_image: 一只手把藏在身后的东西摊到桌上，所有人都看见了
scene: 会议室里，项目拖了几个月，所有人都开始不安。By spring the strain on the small team was manifest to everyone.
sceneCN: 这里 manifest 是「明显的；显而易见的」（第 1 个义项：一眼就能看出、藏不住的状态）；句意：到了春天，这个小团队承受的压力已经人尽皆知。图中可辨识物件：会议室长桌、疲惫的成员、半开的窗帘。

derivatives.zh: manifest 加 -ation 构成，义为「表现；表现形式」
manifest 加 -ly 构成，义为「明显地；显然」
借自意大利语，义为「宣言」；同族词，但经意大利语另成一路
短语，指「昭昭天命」，美国十九世纪的扩张说辞

senses.title: Easy to see and understand
senses.definition: clear and easily noticed or understood, so that no explanation is needed
senses.definitionCN: 清楚、容易被注意或理解，无需多加解释
senses.example: The benefits were manifest within the first month.
senses.exampleCN: 好处在头一个月里就已经很明显了。
senses.why: Latin manifestus described something struck by the hand or caught in the act, that is, plainly there to be seen; that visible quality is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 manifestus 形容「被一只手碰到、当场被抓住」的东西，也就是明明白白摆在那里的东西；「看得见」这一特质是它最老的义项。

senses.title: To show something clearly
senses.definition: to make a feeling, quality, or fact clearly visible to others
senses.definitionCN: 使某种情感、品质或事实清楚地被他人看到
senses.example: The director manifested her anger by ending the meeting early.
senses.exampleCN: 导演以提前散会的方式表明了自己的不满。
senses.why: If manifest means caught in plain sight, the verb is the act of putting something into that sight, from an attitude to a quality.
senses.whyCN: 既然形容词义指「被人一眼看穿」，动词义就是把某种态度或品质放进那道目光之中，使它显现出来。

senses.title: To appear or become visible
senses.definition: to appear in a visible form, especially a quality or condition that becomes noticeable
senses.definitionCN: 以可见的形式出现，尤指某种品质或状况变得引人注意
senses.example: The illness first manifested as a mild fever.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病最初表现为轻微发热。
senses.why: The intransitive use reverses the action: instead of making something show, the thing shows itself, and the word is common in medical talk.
senses.whyCN: 不及物用法把方向倒了过来：不是让人去显示某物，而是某物自己显现出来，因此常见于描写症状与病情。

senses.title: An official cargo list
senses.definition: a detailed list of the goods carried on a ship, aircraft, or truck
senses.definitionCN: 对轮船、飞机或卡车所运货物逐项开列的清单
senses.example: The customs officer compared the manifest with the crates on deck.
senses.exampleCN: 海关官员把载货单与甲板上的货箱逐一核对。
senses.why: The same word came from Italian for a document made public, so the list of goods declared to the authorities took the name.
senses.whyCN: 这个词另一个来自意大利语的面貌指「公之于众的文件」，于是向当局申报货物的清单就被称作 manifest，也就是「把货摊开给人看」。

senses.title: A list of passengers
senses.definition: a list of the people on board a plane or ship
senses.definitionCN: 机上或船上乘客的名册
senses.example: Her name was missing from the flight manifest.
senses.exampleCN: 航班乘客名单上没有她的名字。
senses.why: The cargo list spread to people, because passengers are the other item declared before departure, and rescue teams now rely on the lists to check who is on board.
senses.whyCN: 载货清单扩展到了人身上：乘客才是登机前另一项需要申报的「货物」，如今搜救队也正是靠这份名单核对机上人员。

senses.title: To prove a claim in law
senses.titleCN: 证明；表明（于法律或论证中）
senses.definition: to show clearly that something is true, especially in legal or formal argument
senses.definitionCN: 清楚地表明某事为真，尤见于法律或正式论证
senses.example: The records manifest that the debt was repaid.
senses.exampleCN: 记录证明这笔债务已经偿还。
senses.why: Formal prose extends caught-in-plain-sight to reasons and evidence, so the verb can mean to make a claim plainly evident.
senses.whyCN: 正式文体把「一眼可见」用在理由与证据上，于是动词又能表示让某个主张变得明明白白、无从辩解。

intro.en: Manifest comes from Latin manifestus, plainly evident, probably built from a hand root and a word for striking, and the Latin noun manifestum named a public document.
intro.cn: manifest 来自拉丁语 manifestus（明白可见的），其构成一般认为与「手」和「击打」有关；同族的 manifestum 在中世纪拉丁语里也指公开的文件。

items.en: Manifestus means clearly evident to the senses.
items.cn: manifestus 意为感官上明显可见的。

items.en: The older explanation links manu- (hand) with an old verb for striking or seizing.
items.cn: 较早的一种解释把手（manu-）与古代表击打、扭住的动作联系起来。

items.en: Manifestum can also mean a document made public.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语中 manifestum 也可指公开的文件。

items.en: Manifeste means evident to the eye and to common knowledge.
items.cn: 法语 manifeste 意为肉眼与常识上一清二楚的。

items.en: Manifest enters English as an adjective meaning clearly apparent.
items.cn: manifest 以形容词身份进入英语，义为清楚可见。

items.en: The noun names a public declaration and then a shipping list.
items.cn: 名词形先指公开的声明，随后转指货运清单。

note.en: Manifest is close in form to manifestation and manifestly, and in meaning to obvious and reveal.
note.cn: manifest 形式上与 manifestation、manifestly 同族，意义上则与 obvious、reveal 相邻。

entries.definition: an instance in which something becomes visible
entries.definitionCN: 同一词族的名词，指可见的表现或征兆

entries.definition: in a way that is plain to see
entries.definitionCN: 明显地，由 manifest 加 -ly 构成

entries.definition: a public statement of aims
entries.definitionCN: 宣言；同一来源经意大利语进入英语

entries.definition: easy to see or understand

entries.definition: to make something secret known or visible
entries.definitionCN: 揭示；显露

entries.definition: clearly visible or understood
entries.definitionCN: 明显的；表面上的

normalIntro.en: Manifest is the show-and-see word: what is manifest is out in the open, and to manifest is to put it there.
normalIntro.cn: manifest 是「摊出来给人看」的词：形容词义是已经摆明，动词义是把它摆明。

normal.en: Be manifest in means the evidence can be seen there.
normal.cn: be manifest in 指看得见的证据就在那里。

normal.en: Manifest itself in means something shows up in a certain form.
normal.cn: manifest itself in 指以某种形式显现出来。

normal.en: The adverb manifestly means beyond doubt.
normal.cn: 副词 manifestly 意为毫无疑问地。

normal.en: A flight manifest lists the passengers on board.
normal.cn: flight manifest 列出机上所有乘客。

normal.en: Compare obvious: obvious is everyday, manifest is more formal.
normal.cn: 对比 obvious：obvious 更日常，manifest 更正式。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pulling back a curtain on a hidden box.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把帘子拉开，露出后面的箱子。

abstract.en: See a tired worker rubbing his eyes at the end of a shift.
abstract.cn: 想象一位疲惫的工人下班时揉着双眼。

abstract.en: Imagine a rash spreading on an arm where no one can miss it.
abstract.cn: 想象手臂上冒出疹子，谁都能一眼看到。

examples.en: The results are manifest to anyone who reads the table.
examples.cn: 只要看一眼表格，谁都能看出结果来。

examples.en: The disease first manifests itself as a dry cough.
examples.cn: 这种病最初表现为干咳。

examples.en: The crew checked the cargo manifest before sailing.
examples.cn: 船员在起航前核对了载货单。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「蛮肥似特」——蛮肥的样子特别显眼，一眼就看得见；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 manifestus（明显可见的），一般认为由 manus（手）与表示「击打、扭住」的成分合成，原指「被手抓住、当场可见」；经古法语 manifeste 进入英语，核心义「摊开给人看」。

sensesIntro.en: Manifest moves from plainly visible, to the act of showing and appearing, to the official lists that put goods and passengers in plain view.
sensesIntro.cn: manifest 从「明明白白看得见」出发，延伸到「使之显现」与「自行显现」，再具体成把货物与乘客摊明的官方名单。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand lays what was hidden on the table where all can see.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把藏起来的东西摊到桌上，所有人都看得见。

branches.en: Plainly visible is the oldest and most general sense.
branches.cn: 明显可见是最古老也最一般的义项。

branches.en: Making a feeling or a claim evident puts the adjective into action.
branches.cn: 让情感或主张变得显豁，就是把形容词义变成动作。

branches.en: Something that appears by itself shows the intransitive face.
branches.cn: 自行出现的东西展示了这个词的不及物面目，常用于症状。

branches.en: Official lists put cargo and passengers in plain view of the authorities.
branches.cn: 官方清单把货物与乘客摊在当局眼前。

branches.en: All three describe something escaping from concealment.
branches.cn: 三个义项都在描述某物从藏身处跑了出来。

intro.en: Manifest carries the Latin hand root man- and a Latin ending that has been read as caught or struck.
intro.cn: manifest 带着拉丁语表示手的词根 man-，后缀成分则常被解释为「被抓住、被击中」。

latinIntro.en: Latin manifestus joins a hand root to an old word of striking, and the family also gives manifestum, a public document.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 manifestus 把手与表示击打的古词结合，同族还生出 manifestum（公开文件）。

items.example: The root manu- appears in manual and manifest.
items.exampleCN: 词根 manu- 出现在 manual 与 manifest 中。

items.meaning: struck or seized, according to one explanation
items.meaningCN: 按一种解释，意为「被击打、被抓住」
items.example: The ending -festus is debated among etymologists.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -festus 在词源学者之间有争议。

items.example: Manifestus is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: manifestus 是直接来源。

items.example: Manifestum gives the list sense.
items.exampleCN: manifestum 提供了清单义。

items.example: Manifeste carries the word into French.
items.exampleCN: manifeste 把词带入法语。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms manifestation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 manifestation。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms manifestly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 manifestly。

items.example: The ending -o marks the Italian form manifesto.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -o 标记意大利语形式 manifesto。

items.example: Manifestation describes a visible symptom.
items.exampleCN: manifestation 描述可见的症状。

definition_zh: 操纵他人的；善于操控的；控制欲强的；手法化的
definition_en: skilful at controlling or influencing other people cleverly and often unfairly
core_image: 一双手在幕后悄悄拉线，让木偶照着棋子的路线左右摇摆
scene: 饭桌旁有人不停夸你、套你的话，再顺着你的情绪改变你的主意。His manipulative remarks slowly changed her decision about the job.
sceneCN: 这里 manipulative 是「操纵他人的」（第 1 个义项：用不诚实的手段影响别人的想法或选择）；句意：他那套操控人心的话慢慢改变了她的决定。

pos.zh: 操纵他人的；善于操控的；控制欲强的

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 manipulus 经 manipulate 而来，义为「操纵；操控；熟练处理」
由 manipulate 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「操纵；操控；手法处理」
由 manipulate 加表示人的后缀 -or 构成，义为「操纵者；操控装置」

senses.title: Controlling other people unfairly
senses.titleCN: 操纵他人的；善于操控的
senses.definition: using clever or dishonest methods to make other people think or act as one wants
senses.definitionCN: 用狡猾或不诚实的手段让别人按自己的意愿思考或行动
senses.example: The manager was known for his manipulative style.
senses.exampleCN: 这位经理以善于操控人心而闻名。
senses.why: The Latin hand at work passed from the fairground to the office, so a person who works other people like puppets earns this word.
senses.whyCN: 「用手摆布」的画面从戏台挪到了办公室，把别人当提线木偶摆弄的人，就得到了这个词。

senses.title: Emotionally controlling
senses.definition: behaving in ways that make someone feel guilty, obliged, or afraid in order to control them
senses.definitionCN: 通过让人内疚、欠情或恐惧来达到控制目的的行为
senses.example: Silent treatment is an emotionally manipulative tactic.
senses.exampleCN: 冷处理是操控别人情感的一种手段。
senses.why: Feelings can be handled like objects too, so the hand image shifts from deciding to feeling.
senses.whyCN: 情绪也能像物件一样被拨弄，于是「手」的意象从决定转移到了感受。

senses.title: Hand skilled in handling
senses.titleCN: 手法巧妙的；需要娴熟操作的
senses.definition: needing or showing careful skill with the hands or with tools
senses.definitionCN: 需要或表现出双手或工具操作上的娴熟技巧
senses.example: The surgeon used a steady, manipulative technique.
senses.exampleCN: 这位外科医生用了稳定而熟练的操作手法。
senses.why: The oldest sense kept the literal hand: manipulative as an adjective of manual skill.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项保留了字面上的「手」：作为形容词，表示手上的操作技巧。

senses.title: Rigging in computing
senses.titleCN: 在计算机中操控数据的
senses.definition: in computing, used for directly moving or altering data structures, such as in string manipulation
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机领域指直接移动或修改数据结构，如字符串处理
senses.example: The course teaches manipulative operations on file systems.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课讲授对文件系统的各种操作技法。
senses.why: Digital data are handled by code just as objects are handled by hands.
senses.whyCN: 数字数据由代码来处理，就像物件由双手来处理一样。

senses.title: Skilled treatment of materials
senses.definition: relating to the skilled handling or treatment of physical materials or instruments
senses.definitionCN: 与熟练处理材料或器械相关
senses.example: Clay needs patient, manipulative work before it can be shaped.
senses.exampleCN: 黏土需要耐心反复地揉捏才能成形。
senses.why: Three technical senses grew from manipulative medicine, meaning treatment with hands rather than drugs.
senses.whyCN: 「用手而非药物治病」的手法医学说法，长出了三条技术义项。

senses.title: A follower or practitioner
senses.definition: in older and technical use, a person who handles something, or who practices manual arts
senses.definitionCN: 在较旧与技术性用法中，指动手操作某物的人或从事手工技艺的人
senses.example: The parfumer was recorded among the city manipulative.
senses.exampleCN: 调香师被记在这座城市的手工匠人之中。
senses.why: The -ive ending once also carried agent nouns, so the word named the person who does the handling.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ive 在旧用法里也能构成表示人的名词，于是这个词也指「动手操作的人」。

intro.en: Manipulative comes from French manipulatif and Latin manipulus, a handful, from manus, hand.
intro.cn: manipulative 来自法语 manipulatif 与拉丁语 manipulus（一把），再上溯到 manus（手）。

items.en: Manus means hand, and manipulus means a handful or a small bundle.
items.cn: 拉丁语 manus 意为手，manipulus 意为一把或一小束。

items.en: Manipulare means to handle or to manage something with the hands.
items.cn: manipulare 意为用手处理或管理。

items.en: Manipulatif shapes the adjective from the verb stem.
items.cn: 法语 manipulatif 由动词词干构成形容词。

items.en: Early technical use names surgical and manual treatments.
items.cn: 早期的技术用法指外科与手法治疗。

items.en: The word widens to cover indirect handling of people and affairs.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到间接地摆布他人与事务。

items.en: Modern use makes it a common accusation in psychology and politics.
items.cn: 现代用法使它在心理学与政治评论中成为常见的指责语。

note.en: The first group gathers the manipulus family; the second gathers other words for control and influence.
note.cn: 第一组收 manipulus 词族，第二组收其他表示控制与影响的词。

entries.definition: to handle or control something or someone
entries.definitionCN: 操纵；操控（manipulative 的动词基础词）

entries.definition: the act of handling or controlling
entries.definitionCN: 操纵；操控；手法处理（由 manipulate 加 -ion 构成）

entries.definition: a person who controls others
entries.definitionCN: 操纵者；操控装置（由 manipulate 加 -or 构成）

entries.definition: skilful at getting what one wants by deception
entries.definitionCN: 狡猾的；工于心计的

entries.definition: always wanting to direct how others behave
entries.definitionCN: 控制欲强的；爱支配的

entries.definition: willing to use indirect and dishonest means
entries.definitionCN: 不坦率的；狡诈的

normalIntro.en: Manipulative belongs to the handling family: Latin manus gives us manipulate, manipulation, and the case of the word.
normalIntro.cn: manipulative 属于「动手摆弄」的词族：拉丁语 manus 带来 manipulate、manipulation 以及这个词的「手法」底色。

normal.en: The stem manip- goes back to Latin manus, a hand; anything manipulative is handled by hand.
normal.cn: 词干 manip- 源于拉丁语 manus（手）；凡是 manipulative 的东西都是被「用手摆弄」的。

normal.en: Manipulate is the verb, manipulation the act, and manipulative the adjective for the habit.
normal.cn: manipulate 是动词，manipulation 是行为，manipulative 是形容这种习性的形容词。

normal.en: A manipulative person moves people as a puppeteer moves strings.
normal.cn: 善于操控的人像木偶师拉动丝线一样调动别人。

normal.en: In technical prose it also describes careful handling with hands, as in manipulative surgery.
normal.cn: 在技术文本里它也描述双手的细致操作，如手法外科技艺。

normal.en: Compare cunning: cunning names the trick, manipulative names the habit.
normal.cn: 对比 cunning：cunning 指那个花招，manipulative 指长久的习性。

abstract.en: Picture fingers inside a theatre puppet, lifting its hand to wave.
abstract.cn: 想象剧院木偶里藏着手指，抬起它的手来挥动。

abstract.en: Picture a note passed under the table with a line already written by another person.
abstract.cn: 想象桌下递过一张纸条，上面的话是别人替你写好的。

abstract.en: Picture a florist shaping a stem, always knowing exactly where to bend it.
abstract.cn: 想象花艺师修整花茎，永远知道该在哪里弯折。

examples.en: He denied that his questions were manipulative.
examples.cn: 他否认自己的提问是在操控别人。

examples.en: She left because the relationship had become manipulative.
examples.cn: 她离开了，因为这段关系已经变成操控。

examples.en: Teachers warn parents about manipulative screenshots online.
examples.cn: 教师提醒家长留意网上的操控性截图。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「马尼陪你赌」——一双手在桌底下帮你出牌，表面却像在陪着你；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 manus（手）→ manipulus（一把）→ manipulare（用手处理）→ 法语 manipulatif → 英语 manipulative，核心义「用手摆布」。

sensesIntro.en: Manipulative begins with handling by hand, then handling people, then handling feelings and data, and it finally hardens into a moral judgement.
sensesIntro.cn: manipulative 先指用手操作物件，再指摆布人，然后指操控情绪与数据，最后固化成一种道德评价。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fingers pulling strings behind a puppet stage.
core.cn: 核心意象：舞台后方，几根手指悄悄拉动木偶的丝线。

branches.en: Pulling strings on people is the main accusation sense.
branches.cn: 对他人拉线摆布，是主要的指责义项。

branches.en: Playing on feelings is the intimate version of the same pull.
branches.cn: 拨弄情绪，是同一动作在亲密关系里的版本。

branches.en: Manual skill is the literal hand sense kept from older use.
branches.cn: 手上的技巧，是旧用法保留下来的字面义。

branches.en: Data and materials are handled by code and instruments, keeping the working sense.
branches.cn: 数据与材料由代码和器械处理，延续了「操作」义。

branches.en: Secret control and emotional control both hide the hand behind a friendly face.
branches.cn: 暗中控制与情感控制，都把手藏在友善的面孔后面。

intro.en: Manipulative is built on man- hand plus manipulate, with the adjective ending -ive added to the verb.
intro.cn: manipulative 由表示「手」的 man- 与 manipulate 构成，动词再加形容词后缀 -ive。

latinIntro.en: Latin manus means hand, manipulus means a handful, and manipulare means to handle.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 manus 意为手，manipulus 意为一把，manipulare 意为用手处理。

items.example: Manus is the oldest element of the family.
items.exampleCN: manus 是这个词族最古老的成分。

items.example: Manipulus gives the sense of what a hand can hold.
items.exampleCN: manipulus 给出「一只手能握住的东西」之意。

items.example: Manipulare supplies the action behind manipulate.
items.exampleCN: manipulare 提供 manipulate 背后的动作。

items.example: Manipulate is the base verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: manipulate 是这个词族的基础动词。

items.example: The suffix -ative turns manipulate into manipulative.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ative 把 manipulate 变成 manipulative。

items.example: Manipulative keeps the controlling sense.
items.exampleCN: manipulative 保留了控制义。

items.example: Manipulation adds -ion to the verb.
items.exampleCN: manipulation 由动词加 -ion 构成。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.example: The suffix -or forms manipulator.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -or 构成 manipulator。

items.example: A manipulator is a person who pulls the strings.
items.exampleCN: manipulator 就是那个拉线的人。

definition_zh: 庄园；庄园宅邸；庄园领地；封建采地
definition_en: a large country house with the land and buildings round it, especially the home and estate of a local lord
core_image: 树篱围起的田地和树林中央，立着主人那座大宅，四周是佃农的小屋
scene: 来访者沿着林荫道穿过麦田，终于看见树篱后面那座石砌的大宅。The old manor still owns the woods and the farm beyond the river.
sceneCN: 这里 manor 是「庄园宅邸」（第 1 个义项：作为庄园中心的大宅）；句意：那座老庄园至今还拥有河对岸的树林与农场。

pos.zh: 庄园；庄园宅邸；庄园领地；封建采地

derivatives.zh: 由 manor 加形容词后缀 -ial 构成，义为「庄园的；庄园制的」
由 manor 加 house 构成的合成词，义为「庄园主宅；庄园宅邸」
与 manor 同源于古法语 seigneur（领主），义为「封建领主」

senses.title: The lord great house and land
senses.definition: a large country house with the land and buildings belonging to it
senses.definitionCN: 一座乡村大宅以及属于它的土地和屋舍
senses.example: They restored the manor and opened it to visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 他们修复了这座庄园并对外开放。
senses.why: The Old French word first named the dwelling where a lord held court, so the house itself is the earliest everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 古法语词最初指领主坐镇议事的那座屋宅，因此「大宅本身」是最早最常见的义项。

senses.title: The estate as a whole
senses.definition: the whole estate, including its farms, woods, and villages
senses.definitionCN: 包括农田、树林与村落在内的整片产业
senses.example: The manor employed almost every family in the village.
senses.exampleCN: 这座庄园几乎雇用了村里每一户人家。
senses.why: A dwelling implies what it rules, and soon the whole land attached to the house took the same name.
senses.whyCN: 一座宅邸关联着它所辖的范围，于是与宅邸相连的全部土地也用了同一个词。

senses.title: The feudal land unit
senses.definition: a unit of land held from a feudal lord, with its own court and rights
senses.definitionCN: 向封建领主领有、自带法庭与权利的土地单位
senses.example: Each manor kept its own court for local disputes.
senses.exampleCN: 每个庄园都自设法庭处理本地纠纷。
senses.why: In feudal law the manor was not only ground but a bundle of rights, rents, and jurisdiction.
senses.whyCN: 在封建法里，庄园不只是土地，还捆绑着一整套权利、地租与审判权。

senses.title: The place of lordship
senses.definition: the area in which a lord exercised authority and collected dues
senses.definitionCN: 领主行使权力、征收贡赋的范围
senses.example: Travelers needed permission to cross the manor.
senses.exampleCN: 旅行者穿越这片辖地需要许可。
senses.why: The word shifted from the seat to the reach of the seated power.
senses.whyCN: 词义从「权力所在的位置」转向「权力能够触及的范围」。

senses.title: An American colonial grant
senses.definition: a large grant of land given to a settler in colonial North America
senses.definitionCN: 北美殖民时期授予移民者的大片土地
senses.example: The manor was divided among tenant farmers.
senses.exampleCN: 这片庄园被分给了佃农们。
senses.why: English settlers carried the legal idea across the Atlantic and applied it to new land grants.
senses.whyCN: 英国移民把这个法律概念带过大西洋，用在新的土地授给制度上。

senses.title: Police district in New York
senses.definition: in New York City, a police district
senses.definitionCN: 纽约市的警察管辖区
senses.example: The call was sent to the manor on duty.
senses.exampleCN: 这通报警被转给了值班的辖区警局。
senses.why: The idea of a bounded territory of authority easily stretched from a lord to a police station.
senses.whyCN: 「有边界的一块管辖领地」这个概念很容易从领主延伸到警察局。

senses.title: A small run-down house
senses.definition: loosely, a modest or run-down house, often said with irony
senses.definitionCN: 口语中随意指一座普通或破旧的房子，常带反讽
senses.example: The couple called their one-room flat a grand manor.
senses.exampleCN: 这对夫妇把单间公寓称作气派的大庄园。
senses.why: Calling a small shelter a manor plays on the gap between grand landholding and a single room.
senses.whyCN: 把小住处叫作庄园，玩的正是「大片地产」与「一间房」之间的落差。

intro.en: Manor comes through Old French manoir, a dwelling, from Latin manere, to remain.
intro.cn: manor 经古法语 manoir（住处）而来，源于拉丁语 manere（停留、居住）。

items.en: Manere means to remain or to stay, and gives dwelling words across Europe.
items.cn: 拉丁语 manere 意为停留、居住，为欧洲多种语言提供了「住处」类词。

items.en: Mansio names a stopping place and mansionem a staying or abode.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 mansio 指歇脚的处所，mansionem 指停留或居所。

items.en: Manoir and maner mean a dwelling place, and manoir is the home of a seigneur.
items.cn: 古法语 manoir 与 maner 意为住处，manoir 也指领主的宅邸。

items.en: Maner appears in legal and estate use as the land unit of a lord.
items.cn: 中古英语 maner 在法律与地产文书中指领主的土地单位。

items.en: The spelling settles as manor and the word divides from mansion.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 manor，并与 mansion 分道扬镳。

items.en: The manor becomes a country house visited by tourists and a police district in New York.
items.cn: 庄园成为游客参观的乡间宅邸，在纽约又指警察辖区。

note.en: The first group shows the manere family with the two children manor and mansion; the second gathers other words for estates and grand homes.
note.cn: 第一组展示 manere 词族及其两个分支 manor 与 mansion；第二组收其他表示庄园与豪宅的词。

entries.definition: relating to a manor
entries.definitionCN: 庄园的；庄园制的（由 manor 加 -ial 构成）

entries.definition: a very large impressive house
entries.definitionCN: 大厦；豪宅（与 manor 同源于 manere，侧重宅邸的宏大）

entries.definition: the house provided for a minister
entries.definitionCN: 牧师住宅（与 manor 同源于 manere，只是拼写相近，词义侧重教职住宅）

entries.definition: a large area of land owned by one person or family
entries.definitionCN: 地产；庄园产业

entries.definition: a very large house
entries.definitionCN: 豪宅；大厦

entries.definition: a large house in the countryside, often historic
entries.definitionCN: 乡间大宅；乡村庄园宅邸

normalIntro.en: Manor is a staying place: Latin manere gives the family, and the Old French dwelling word shaped this one.
normalIntro.cn: manor 是「停留之处」：拉丁语 manere 给出这个词族，古法语中的「住处」词塑造了它。

normal.en: The root man- here means to stay, as in manere, not the man- of manual.
normal.cn: 这里的词根 man- 表示「停留」（来自 manere），不是 manual 里的「手」。

normal.en: Manor and mansion are cousins from manere; the manor is the land and the house that rules it.
normal.cn: manor 与 mansion 是 manere 的同族：庄园是那片土地及统辖它的宅邸。

normal.en: The lord of the manor held a court, so the word belongs to law as much as to scenery.
normal.cn: 庄园领主自设法庭，所以这个词既属于风景也属于法律。

normal.en: Manorial is the adjective: manorial rights, manorial records.
normal.cn: manorial 是它的形容词：庄园权利、庄园档案。

normal.en: Compare estate: an estate is land and property, a manor also carries the lord and the court.
normal.cn: 对比 estate：estate 是土地与财产，manor 还带着领主与法庭。

abstract.en: See a stone gate at the end of a long drive, with fields on every side.
abstract.cn: 想象长长的车道尽头有一道石门，四周全是田野。

abstract.en: See a map with one shaded ring drawn around a big house and four small farms.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，在大宅和四座小农场外面画着一个阴影圈。

abstract.en: See a raised hand in an old hall that settles every quarrel over a boundary.
abstract.cn: 想象在旧时的大厅里，一只举起的手裁定了每一场地界纠纷。

examples.en: The manor sits on a hill above the river.
examples.cn: 庄园坐落在河上方的山坡上。

examples.en: Records of the manor go back to the thirteenth century.
examples.cn: 这座庄园的档案可追溯到十三世纪。

examples.en: Two manors shared the same church.
examples.cn: 两个庄园共用同一座教堂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「马诺儿」——一位叫马诺的领主骑在马上巡查自家田地；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 manere（停留、居住）→ 晚期拉丁语 mansio（居所）→ 古法语 manoir（领主宅邸）→ 英语 manor（庄园），核心义「领主停留并统辖的那片土地与大宅」。

sensesIntro.en: Manor starts as the lord dwelling, spreads to the whole estate and its legal rights, and then travels to colonial land and even to police districts.
sensesIntro.cn: manor 从领主的宅邸开始，扩展到整片产业及其法律权利，又漂洋过海用于殖民地授地，甚至指警察辖区。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a great house at the centre of hedged fields, with tenant cottages around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：树篱围绕的田地中央立着一座大宅，四周散布着佃农的小屋。

branches.en: The house itself is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 大宅本身是日常使用的义项。

branches.en: The land around the house is the estate sense.
branches.cn: 宅邸周边的土地是产业义项。

branches.en: Feudal law turns the estate into a unit of rights and jurisdiction.
branches.cn: 封建法把庄园变成一条权利与审判权的单位。

branches.en: Colonial grants and police districts reuse the bounded-territory idea.
branches.cn: 殖民地授地与警察辖区沿用了「有界领地」的思路。

branches.en: A grand landed house and a joke about a small flat both measure the same gap.
branches.cn: 气派的庄园大宅与拿小房子开玩笑，测的是同一道反差。

intro.en: Manor is built on the Latin root man-, meaning to remain, with the Old French -oir ending of place nouns.
intro.cn: manor 建立在表示「停留」的拉丁词根 man- 上，加上古法语表示处所的名词词尾 -oir。

latinIntro.en: Latin manere means to remain, mansio a stopping place, and mansionem an abode.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 manere 意为停留，mansio 意为留宿处，mansionem 意为居所。

items.example: Manere is the root behind dwelling words.
items.exampleCN: manere 是这些「住处」词的共同词根。

items.example: Mansio names where a traveller stays.
items.exampleCN: mansio 指旅人停留的地方。

items.example: Manoir is the direct source of manor.
items.exampleCN: manoir 是 manor 的直接来源。

items.example: Manor keeps the landed sense.
items.exampleCN: manor 保留了「田产」义。

items.example: The suffix -oire forms words of place.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -oire 构成表示处所的词。

items.example: The suffix -ial forms manorial.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ial 构成 manorial。

items.example: Manorial describes rights and records of a manor.
items.exampleCN: manorial 描述庄园的权利与档案。

items.example: Mansion is a cousin from the same root.
items.exampleCN: mansion 是同根的近亲词。

items.example: Manse also comes from manere.
items.exampleCN: manse 也来自 manere。

definition_zh: 大厦；豪宅；大宅；公寓大楼
definition_en: a very large and impressive house
core_image: 石阶尽头两扇巨大的门，门后一长排房间，灯光一层层亮到屋顶
scene: 车子驶进富人区，路两边都是高大的宅子。They bought a mansion with twelve bedrooms and a garden the size of a park.
sceneCN: 这里 mansion 是「大厦、豪宅」（第 1 个义项：巨大而气派的住宅）；句意：他们买下一座有十二间卧室、花园大得像公园的豪宅。

pos.zh: 大厦；豪宅；大宅；公寓大楼

derivatives.zh: 与 mansion 同源于拉丁语 manere，义为「牧师住宅；宅邸」
与 mansion 同源于 manere，经 manor 加 -ial 构成，义为「庄园的」
由 mansion 加指小后缀 -ette 构成，义为「小型宅第；小屋式公寓」

senses.title: A very large impressive house
senses.definition: a very large and impressive house, often one with many rooms
senses.definitionCN: 一座非常巨大而气派的住宅，往往房间众多
senses.example: The old mansion has forty rooms and a private chapel.
senses.exampleCN: 这座旧宅邸有四十个房间和一间私人礼拜堂。
senses.why: The Latin word began as a place to stay, and a wealthy staying place naturally grew tall and wide.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词本指「停留之处」，而富人的停留之处自然越长越高大宽敞。

senses.title: The great house of an estate
senses.titleCN: 庄园主宅；统辖田产的大宅
senses.definition: the principal house of an estate or of a noble family
senses.definitionCN: 田产或贵族家族的主要住宅
senses.example: The family mansion stood at the end of the drive.
senses.exampleCN: 家族的宅邸立在车道尽头。
senses.why: In older use mansion was the home seat of a lord, so the house and the land it headed share the idea.
senses.whyCN: 旧用法中 mansion 是领主的正宅，于是宅邸与它所统辖的土地共享同一个概念。

senses.title: A building divided into flats
senses.definition: in British use, a large building divided into flats, as in a mansion block
senses.definitionCN: 英式用法中指分隔成多套公寓的大楼，如 mansion block
senses.example: They live in a Victorian mansion block near the park.
senses.exampleCN: 他们住在公园附近一栋维多利亚式公寓大楼里。
senses.why: A single great house that once sheltered one family was cut into many dwellings, carrying its name along.
senses.whyCN: 一座原本只住一户人家的大宅被分隔成许多住处，却把原名的招牌留了下来。

senses.title: A lodging plane in astrology
senses.definition: in astrology, one of the twelve bands of the zodiac, each ruled by a sign, called a mansion
senses.definitionCN: 占星术中黄道上的区段，以星座为界，称为「宿」
senses.example: Medieval astrologers listed the moon mansions.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪的占星家列出了月宿。
senses.why: The staying place became a place in the sky where the moon pauses night after night.
senses.whyCN: 「停留之处」被搬到天上，成了月亮夜夜歇脚的「宿」。

senses.title: A dwelling place
senses.definition: archaic use for any dwelling place or abode
senses.definitionCN: 古旧用法，泛指任何住处或居所
senses.example: The psalm speaks of lasting mansions in the heavens.
senses.exampleCN: 诗篇里说到天上恒久的居所。
senses.why: Before it meant grandeur, mansion simply named where a person stays.
senses.whyCN: 在表示气派之前，mansion 只是指人停留的地方。

senses.title: An impressive building
senses.definition: in looser use, any large stately building, such as a hospital or museum
senses.definitionCN: 较宽松的用法中，指任何宏大庄严的建筑，如医院或博物馆
senses.example: The hospital was housed in a baroque mansion.
senses.exampleCN: 这家医院设在一座巴洛克式的宏伟建筑里。
senses.why: When the building is grand enough, its function matters less than its size.
senses.whyCN: 建筑一旦足够气派，用途就被尺寸盖过，也能叫 mansion。

intro.en: Mansion comes through Old French from Latin mansio and mansionem, a staying or an abode, from manere, to remain.
intro.cn: mansion 经古法语来自拉丁语 mansio 与 mansionem（停留、居所），源于 manere（停留）。

items.en: Manere means to remain, and mansio means a staying or a stopping place.
items.cn: 拉丁语 manere 意为停留，mansio 意为停留或歇脚处。

items.en: Mansio extends to a station on a road or a night lodging.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 mansio 扩展到驿道上的驿站或夜间住处。

items.en: Maison and mansion name a house or a dwelling place.
items.cn: 古法语 maison 与 mansion 指房屋或住处。

items.en: Mansioun means an abode, and later a large house.
items.cn: 中古英语 mansioun 指居所，后来指大宅。

items.en: The word is applied to grand town and country houses.
items.cn: 这个词被用来指城里和乡下的豪宅。

items.en: Mansion now means luxury housing and, in Britain, a block of flats.
items.cn: 现代英语 mansion 指豪华住宅，在英式英语中又指公寓大楼。

note.en: The first group shows forms from the manere family; the second gathers other words for very large homes.
note.cn: 第一组展示 manere 词族中的成员；第二组收其他表示巨大住宅的词。

entries.definition: the house of a minister
entries.definitionCN: 牧师住宅（与 mansion 同源于 manere，拼写相近但短得多）

entries.definition: a lord house and its land
entries.definitionCN: 庄园；庄园宅邸（与 mansion 同源于 manere，侧重田产）

entries.definition: relating to a manor
entries.definitionCN: 庄园的（由 manor 加 -ial 构成，与 mansion 同根）

entries.definition: the official home of a king or queen
entries.definitionCN: 宫殿；王宫

entries.definition: a large house in the country or by the sea

entries.definition: a French country house or castle

normalIntro.en: Mansion is a staying place grown grand: Latin manere gives the root, and -sion marks a noun of place or action.
normalIntro.cn: mansion 是变得堂皇的「停留之处」：拉丁语 manere 提供词根，-sion 标记处所或行为名词。

normal.en: The manc- and man- part goes back to manere, to stay, as in permanent and remain.
normal.cn: manc- 与 man- 这部分源自 manere（停留），如同 permanent 与 remain。

normal.en: Mansion and manor are cousins from the same root; mansion emphasises the great house, manor the land.
normal.cn: mansion 与 manor 是同一词根的同族词：mansion 强调大宅，manor 强调土地。

normal.en: The -sion ending appears in place and action nouns such as mansion and mission.
normal.cn: 后缀 -sion 常见于处所与行为名词，如 mansion 与 mission。

normal.en: A mansion block is a British building of flats, so the word need not mean one family.
normal.cn: mansion block 是英式的公寓大楼，所以这个词并不一定指一户人家。

normal.en: Compare villa: a villa is a fine house, a mansion is a house of very great size.
normal.cn: 对比 villa：villa 是精致住宅，mansion 是尺寸极其巨大的宅子。

abstract.en: See a marble staircase where a single step holds your whole family.
abstract.cn: 想象一段大理石台阶，一级就宽得能站下全家。

abstract.en: See a chandelier so high that the ceiling disappears above it.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏吊灯高得让天花板在它上面都看不见了。

abstract.en: See one old front door that has been split into six bell buttons.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇古典大门被改成挂着六个门铃的合用入口。

examples.en: The novelist grew up in a crumbling mansion.
examples.cn: 这位小说家在一座破败的大宅里长大。

examples.en: Several mansions line the avenue.
examples.cn: 这条大道两旁排列着好几座豪宅。

examples.en: The city turned the mansion into a museum.
examples.cn: 市里把这座大宅改成了博物馆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「蠻神」——像住着大力神的房子，大到要神才撑得起；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 manere（停留）→ 拉丁语 mansio、mansionem（停留；居所）→ 古法语 maison、mansion → 英语 mansion，核心义「宏大而气派的居住之所」。

sensesIntro.en: Mansion starts as any place to stay, narrows into the great house of the rich, and then widens again to flats and stately buildings.
sensesIntro.cn: mansion 先泛指任何停留之处，收缩为富人的巨大宅邸，再扩展为公寓大楼与宏伟建筑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a great stone house with rows of windows and a long flight of steps.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座石砌大宅，窗户排成长长几排，门前是一段很高的台阶。

branches.en: The huge impressive house is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 巨大气派的住宅是日常义项。

branches.en: The family seat with land is the older estate sense.
branches.cn: 带有田产的家族正宅是较旧的产业义项。

branches.en: Flats and grand public buildings reuse the size without the wealth.
branches.cn: 公寓大楼与宏伟公共建筑沿用了尺寸，却不带财力。

branches.en: A lodging in the sky and a plain abode keep the plain staying sense.
branches.cn: 天上的「宿」与朴素的居所，保留了「停留」的原义。

branches.en: A luxury house and a lord great house both stand at the top of a social ladder.
branches.cn: 豪宅与领主大宅都站在社会阶梯的顶端。

intro.en: Mansion is built on the Latin root man-, to remain, with the noun ending -sion for a place or act.
intro.cn: mansion 建立在表示「停留」的拉丁词根 man- 上，加上表示处所或行为的名词词尾 -sion。

latinIntro.en: Latin manere means to remain, mansio a staying, and mansionem an abode.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 manere 意为停留，mansio 意为停留，mansionem 意为居所。

items.example: Manere is the root of mansioun.
items.exampleCN: manere 是中古英语 mansioun 的词根。

items.example: Mansio gave the shape mans-.
items.exampleCN: mansio 给出 mans- 这个词形。

items.example: Mansionem is the accusative passed into Old French.
items.exampleCN: mansionem 是传入古法语的宾格形式。

items.example: Mansion keeps the dwelling sense.
items.exampleCN: mansion 保留了居所义。

items.meaning: forming nouns of place or action
items.example: The suffix -sion appears in mansion and mansion-house.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -sion 出现在 mansion 与 mansion-house 中。

items.example: Manse comes from the same Latin root.
items.exampleCN: manse 来自同一拉丁词根。

items.example: Manor is the landed cousin of mansion.
items.exampleCN: manor 是 mansion 的「土地版」近亲。

items.example: Manorial comes from manor through -ial.
items.exampleCN: manorial 由 manor 加 -ial 构成。

items.example: The suffix -ette forms mansionette.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ette 构成 mansionette。

items.example: A mansionette is a small, flat-like home.
items.exampleCN: mansionette 是形状接近公寓的小住宅。

definition_zh: 大理石；大理石制品；弹珠；弹珠游戏；云纹；使……带大理石纹理
definition_en: a hard stone with coloured veins that takes a high polish, or a small glass ball children play with; also to give something a vein-like pattern
core_image: 一块被打磨得锃亮的白石，表面游走着灰色的纹理，握在手里冰凉
scene: 古庙的台阶被风雨磨得发亮，石面上还看得见淡灰色的波纹。The old temple steps are made of white marble veined with grey.
sceneCN: 这里 marble 是「大理石」（第 1 个义项：打磨后能泛出光泽的石灰岩）；句意：古庙的台阶由带灰色纹理的白色大理石砌成。图中可辨认的物件有台阶、石柱与石缝里的青苔。

pos.zh: 大理石；大理石雕像或制品；弹珠；弹珠游戏
使……带上大理石般的纹理；给……染色成大理石花纹

collocations.zh: 大理石蛋糕（深浅两色相间）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「有大理石花纹的；带纹理的」，如 marbled paper 大理石纹纸
由本词加 -y 构成，义为「大理石般的；像大理石一样冰冷坚硬的」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「大理石花纹；肥肉里的肌间脂肪纹」
由 marbled 与 paper 复合而成，义为「大理石纹纸」，旧时多用于书封与活页

senses.title: The veined polished stone
senses.definition: a hard limestone that can be smoothed to a shine, usually white or pale with coloured veins running through it
senses.definitionCN: 一种可以打磨出光泽的坚硬石灰岩，多为白色或浅色，内部夹有彩色纹理
senses.example: The cathedral floor is paved with white marble from the quarries north of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 大教堂的地面铺着城北采石场出产的白色大理石。
senses.why: Greek marmaros meant any gleaming stone; the sense narrowed to the stone that takes a high polish, and that material is the core sense.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 marmaros 泛指发亮的石头，后来收窄到能被打磨得发亮的这一种；材料本身正是最核心的义项。

senses.title: Something carved from marble
senses.definition: a statue or a piece of carved work made from this stone, usually in a museum or public square
senses.definitionCN: 用大理石雕成的雕像或构件，多见于博物馆或公共广场
senses.example: The museum keeps a marble of the emperor as a young man.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆藏有一尊青年皇帝时期的大理石雕像。
senses.why: By metonymy the name of the material stands for the object cut from it, so a marble can be a solid carved figure you can walk around.
senses.whyCN: 这里由材料代指成品：用大理石雕出的东西本身就叫 marble，所以一尊可绕行观赏的雕像可以被称为一个 marble。

senses.title: The glass ball children play with
senses.definition: a small ball of glass or stone, often with colour inside, used in a children game of flicking them at one another
senses.definitionCN: 玻璃或石头做的小圆球，内部常有彩纹，用于小孩互相弹射的游戏
senses.example: He flicked the red marble across the dusty ground and knocked two others out of the ring.
senses.exampleCN: 他把那颗红色弹珠弹过满是尘土的地面，撞飞了圈里的另外两颗。
senses.why: Glass balls were polished till they shone like small pieces of marble, so the children game borrowed the stone name for its little ball.
senses.whyCN: 玻璃球被磨得发亮，活像一小块大理石，于是弹珠游戏就把石头的名字挪给了小球，生出这个义项。

senses.title: The children game itself
senses.definition: the game in which players shoot these small balls in turn, with the loser giving up the ball
senses.definitionCN: 玩家轮流弹射这些小球的游戏，输的一方要把球交给对方
senses.example: After school the boys played marbles in the yard until the light failed.
senses.exampleCN: 放学后男孩子们在院子里玩弹珠，一直玩到天色暗下来。
senses.why: English turns the name of a game piece into the name of the game simply by adding a plural, so marbles can mean the whole activity.
senses.whyCN: 英语只要把棋子名变成复数就能指整项活动，所以 marbles 也就表示整场弹珠游戏，这一义项由此而来。

senses.title: Veins of colour like stone
senses.titleCN: 大理石般的云纹与花纹
senses.definition: a pattern of thin curving streaks, especially of fat in meat or colours in paper and pastry, that looks like the veins of polished stone
senses.definitionCN: 细长弯曲的纹路，如肉里夹的脂肪纹，或纸与点心上的色纹，形似打磨后石头的纹理
senses.example: The butcher pointed to the fine marble running through the cut of beef.
senses.exampleCN: 屠夫指着一块牛肉里细细夹着的雪花纹理。
senses.why: Once the stone image is fixed in the mind, any thin winding streak recalls it, so the word names the pattern by analogy.
senses.whyCN: 石头的形象一旦固定下来，任何细长蜿蜒的纹路都会让人想起它，于是这个词就通过类比来指这种花纹。

senses.title: To stain with stone-like veins
senses.definition: to colour paper, cloth, a book edge or dough so that it shows curling veins like those of marble
senses.definitionCN: 把纸、布、书边或面团染出弯曲的纹路，如同大理石上的纹理
senses.example: The workshop marbles paper by floating ink on water and laying the sheet onto it.
senses.exampleCN: 作坊在水面上浮一层墨，再把纸铺上去，以此给纸染出大理石花纹。
senses.why: The verb turns the visible pattern into an action: making the stone image appear on any flat surface.
senses.whyCN: 动词把看得见的花纹变成动作：让石头的形象出现在任何平整的表面上。

senses.title: Cold and hard like stone
senses.titleCN: 像大理石一样冰冷坚硬
senses.definition: in phrases such as marble-hearted or as cold as marble, describing something unfeeling or rigidly hard
senses.definitionCN: 用于 marble-hearted、as cold as marble 等短语，形容冷酷无情或坚硬如石
senses.example: The marble heart of the old landlord never softened, even when the rent was all they had.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老房东铁石般的心从未软过，即使租金已是他们仅有的东西。
senses.why: The stone keeps what is set in it and stays cold to the touch, so the material easily serves as a metaphor for hardness of feeling.
senses.whyCN: 这种石头保持原样、摸上去又冷，所以材料很容易被拿来做情感坚硬的比喻，这一义项就由此长出来。

senses.title: Marbles: the wits of a person
senses.titleCN: 弹珠：指人的头脑与理智
senses.definition: in the informal phrases lose your marbles and have all your marbles, the glass balls stand for a clear mind
senses.definitionCN: 在口语短语 lose your marbles、have all your marbles 中，玻璃球被用来比喻清醒的头脑
senses.example: The long weeks of heat made him lose his marbles, and he began talking to the pigeons.
senses.exampleCN: 接连数周的高温让他失去了理智，开始对着鸽子说话。
senses.why: A loose marble rolls away and cannot be recalled, so when the glass balls are lost the mind is said to be lost with them.
senses.whyCN: 松脱的弹珠会滚走再也找不回，于是人们便说弹珠丢了，头脑也跟着丢了，这就是这个口语义项的由来。

intro.en: Marble comes from Greek marmaros, a shining stone, through Latin marmor and Old French marbre; the deeper Indo-European root is much debated.
intro.cn: marble 出自希腊语 marmaros（发亮的石头），经拉丁语 marmor 与古法语 marbre 进入英语；更早的印欧语词根争议很大。

items.en: Greek marmaros named a bright, gleaming stone; its origin is debated, and many scholars connect it with marmairein, to flash or sparkle.
items.cn: 希腊语 marmaros 指发亮、闪光的石头；其来源有争议，许多学者把它与动词「闪耀、闪光」联系起来。

items.en: Latin marmor named the stone itself and any vessel or slab cut from it.
items.cn: 拉丁语 marmor 既指石头本身，也指用这种石头做成的器皿或石板。

items.en: Old French marbre carried the word towards English, and the word still shows the French stress and the short final syllable.
items.cn: 古法语 marbre 把词带向英语，英语至今仍保留法语的读法与结尾的短音节。

items.en: Middle English used marble for the building stone; its earliest recorded use in written English is uncertain in date.
items.cn: 中古英语用 marble 指这种建筑石材；它在书面英语中的最早出现年代不确定。

items.en: Polished glass balls became marble-shaped playthings and took the name; the paper-staining craft later gave the related verb and adjective.
items.cn: 磨光的玻璃球成了弹珠玩具并借用了这个名称；后来的染纸工艺又给这个词带来了相关动词与形容词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with the same Latin stone root or the same spelling shape; the near-meaning group gathers other stones and surfaces people mistake for marble.
note.cn: 形近组收同出一个拉丁石头的词根的词，以及与它拼写相像的词；近义组收常被误当作大理石的其他石材与表面。

entries.definition: to paint or stain a surface with veins so that it looks like marble
entries.definitionCN: 在表面上画出或染出纹理，使其看起来像大理石。由本词加动词后缀构成

entries.definition: marked with curling veins that look like polished stone
entries.definitionCN: 带有弯曲纹理的，纹路像打磨过的石头。由本词加 -ed 构成

entries.definition: the plural of the noun, used for the glass balls and for the game played with them
entries.definitionCN: 本词的复数形式，可指多颗弹珠，也可指用弹珠玩的游戏

entries.definition: a very hard grey stone made of grains, commonly used for worktops and steps
entries.definitionCN: 由颗粒构成的坚硬灰色岩石，常用于台面与台阶，比大理石耐磨也更不透明

entries.definition: a softer pale stone from which marble is formed when heat and pressure harden it
entries.definitionCN: 一种较软的浅色石材，在高温高压下变质后即成为大理石

entries.definition: shiny and smooth on the surface, as polished marble is
entries.definitionCN: 表面光亮平滑的，就像打磨过的大理石

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the real Greek stone root and the phrases in which marble actually appears.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子依据真实的希腊石头词根，以及 marble 实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Greek marmaros meant a gleaming stone, so marble is the stone that shines after polishing.
normal.cn: 希腊语 marmaros 意为发亮的石头，所以 marble 就是打磨后能发亮的那种石头。

normal.en: Marble spent its early life in the quarry as limestone, hardened by heat and pressure.
normal.cn: 大理石在采石场里年轻时是石灰岩，受热受压之后才变硬成形。

normal.en: To lose your marbles is to lose the little glass balls that stand for a clear mind.
normal.cn: lose your marbles 就是弄丢了那些代表清醒头脑的小玻璃球。

normal.en: A marble cake or a marbled sheet has curling veins, named after the veins in polished stone.
normal.cn: 大理石蛋糕或大理石纹纸都有弯曲纹路，命名取自打磨后石头里的纹路。

normal.en: A statue in a museum is often simply called a marble, because the material stands for the carved thing.
normal.cn: 博物馆里的雕像常被直接叫作 a marble，因为材料代指雕成的成品。

abstract.en: Picture a slab of white stone with grey rivers frozen inside it, each straight line of a river a vein of colour.
abstract.cn: 想象一块白石板，里面冻着灰色的河流，每一条河都是彩色的纹脉。

abstract.en: A hand chisels a figure out of that slab, and what was stone becomes a white robed body on a pedestal.
abstract.cn: 一只手从那块石板上凿出人形，石头变成了基座上穿白袍的身躯。

abstract.en: A child flicks a tiny polished glass ball across the dust; it is marble-sized and marble-bright.
abstract.cn: 孩子把一颗磨光的小玻璃球弹过尘土，它大小如弹珠、亮如大理石。

examples.en: The hotel lobby has a marble floor that reflects the chandeliers.
examples.cn: 酒店大堂的大理石地板映出吊灯的光。

examples.en: The children hid their marbles in a tin box under the bed.
examples.cn: 孩子们把弹珠藏在床底下的铁盒里。

examples.en: Bakers marble the two batters gently so that the colours stay distinct.
examples.cn: 面包师把两种面糊轻轻搅出大理石花纹，让颜色保持分明。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「抹布」——抹布一遍遍擦过石面，把白石擦得发亮，这就是大理石；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 marmaros「发亮的石头」→ 拉丁语 marmor「大理石」→ 古法语 marbre → 英语 marble；希腊语更早的来源有争议，一般认为与「闪耀、闪光」有关，属重构推测。

sensesIntro.en: Marble starts from a gleaming polished stone, branches into the carved object and the polished glass ball, then into the game, the vein pattern, the craft of staining, the cold hard metaphor and the lost mind.
sensesIntro.cn: marble 从一块打磨发亮的石头出发，先分出雕成的成品与磨光的玻璃球，再延伸到弹珠游戏、石材般的纹路、染纹工艺、冰冷坚硬的比喻，以及丢掉的理智。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a polished white stone slab with grey rivers of vein running through it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块打磨发亮的白石板，灰色纹理像河流在石中穿行。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL: the polished veined stone, the pattern it shows, and the craft of staining other surfaces to match.
branches.cn: 材料线：打磨出纹理的石头本身、它显现的花纹，以及把别的表面染成同样花纹的手艺。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: by name transfer, the material stands for the statue carved out of it.
branches.cn: 成品线：借名称转移，材料代指从中雕出的雕像。

branches.en: THE PLAYTHING: the polished glass ball borrowed the stone name, and the plural names the game.
branches.cn: 玩物线：磨光的玻璃球借用了石头的名字，复数形式又指整场游戏。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: the coldness and firmness of stone become an image for an unfeeling heart.
branches.cn: 比喻线：石头冰冷坚硬的特质成为无情之心的形象。

branches.en: THE SPOKEN IMAGE: lost glass balls stand for a lost mind in everyday speech.
branches.cn: 口语线：在口语里，丢失的玻璃球成了丢失理智的形象。

intro.en: Marble comes from a Greek stone word that reached English through Latin and French; English then adds its own suffixes to name the pattern and the craft.
intro.cn: marble 来自希腊语的石头词，经拉丁语与法语进入英语；英语再用自己的后缀为花纹与手艺造出新词。

latinIntro.en: Latin marmor is the recorded stepping stone between Greek marmaros and the French form that English borrowed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 marmor 是希腊语 marmaros 与英语所借的法语形式之间确有记录的中转站。

items.example: Marmaros lies behind every later form of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词后来的每一种形式都出自 marmaros。

items.meaning: marble; a slab or vessel of marble
items.meaningCN: 大理石；大理石石板或器皿
items.example: Latin marmor is the direct ancestor of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 marmor 是英语本词的直接祖先。

items.example: French shortened the word before English took it.
items.exampleCN: 英语借入之前，法语已把这词缩短过。

items.example: The steps were cut from solid marble.
items.exampleCN: 台阶是用整块大理石凿成的。

items.example: The ending -ed forms marbled.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 marbled。

items.meaningCN: 带石纹的；大理石花纹的
items.example: They bound the books in red marbled paper.
items.exampleCN: 他们用红色大理石纹纸装订这些书。

items.example: The ending -ing forms marbling.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 marbling。

items.example: The suffix -y forms marbly.

latinEntries.meaning: marble; a slab or vessel of marble
latinEntries.meaningCN: 大理石；大理石石板或器皿
大理石做的；白如大理石的

definition_zh: 记号笔；标记物；路标；分数线；标志性特征；记分员
definition_en: an object, sign or pen used to show where something is or to label it, or a number that fixes the level a standard is set at
core_image: 道旁竖起的一根漆着颜色的木桩，在草地里划出界线，让人一眼看见位置
scene: 马拉松选手跑到岔路口，路边立着一块醒目的指示牌，箭头指向弯道。A tall marker beside the track points runners towards the bend.
sceneCN: 这里 marker 是「标记物；指示牌」（第 2 个义项：用来标示位置或方向的物件）；句意：赛道旁一块高高的指示牌把跑者引向弯道。图中可辨认的物件有指示牌、箭头和跑道边的草地。

pos.zh: 记号笔；标记物；路标；分数线；标志性特征；记分员

collocations.zh: 油性记号笔；不褪色记号笔

derivatives.zh: 由动词 mark 加 -ed 构成，义为「显著的；明显的」，与 marker 共用同一个动词词根
由 marked 加 -ly 构成，义为「明显地；显著地」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「标记；斑纹；评分」，与 marker 共享「做记号」这一核心动作
由 land 与 mark 复合而成，义为「地标；里程碑」，是 marker 的具体复合形式
由 post 与 mark 复合而成，义为「邮戳」，属于同一词族的复合词

senses.title: The pen that writes in thick ink
senses.definition: a thick pen with a felt tip and strong ink, used to write on board, cardboard or plastic
senses.definitionCN: 带毡头的粗笔，墨水浓重，用来在黑板上、纸板上或塑料上书写
senses.example: She wrote the price on the box with a black marker.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一支黑色记号笔把价格写在箱子上。
senses.why: A marker is literally a thing that marks, and of all marking tools the thick felt pen is the one whose whole job is to leave an easy-to-see mark.
senses.whyCN: marker 字面就是「做记号的东西」，而在各种标记工具中，粗毡头笔的全部用途正是留下便于看见的记号，因此首先得到这一义项。

senses.title: An object that shows a place
senses.definition: a post, sign, stone or floating object set in a place to show where something is or where a boundary runs
senses.definitionCN: 插在某处的木桩、牌子、石块或浮标，用来标示某物所在或边界的走向
senses.example: The hikers followed the orange markers along the ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 徒步者沿着山脊上的橙色路标前行。
senses.why: The same job is done by an object instead of a pen: something stands in a place and says, this is the spot.
senses.whyCN: 同样的工作改由物件来完成：某样东西立在某个位置，就等于宣布「就是这里」。

senses.title: A level that sets a standard
senses.definition: a score, figure or level that must be reached before a test counts as passed or a disease counts as present
senses.definitionCN: 必须达到的分数、数值或水平，达到才算通过考试或判定为患病
senses.example: Fewer than half the candidates reached the pass marker this year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年不到一半的考生达到了及格线。
senses.why: A marker in the ground fixes a line; applied to numbers, the same word fixes the line between pass and fail.
senses.whyCN: 立在地上的标桩固定出一条线；这个意思挪到数字上，就成了及格与不及格之间的那条线。

senses.title: A sign that shows a process
senses.definition: a feature or measure that shows the state of something, such as health, progress or social change
senses.definitionCN: 能显示某事物状态的特征或衡量标准，如健康状况、进展或社会变化
senses.example: Rising test scores are a marker of better teaching in these schools.
senses.exampleCN: 考试成绩上升是这些学校教学质量提高的标志。
senses.why: What is marked can be invisible, so a visible sign becomes the marker of a hidden process.
senses.whyCN: 被标记的东西可以看不见，于是一个看得见的迹象就成了某个隐藏过程的标志。

senses.title: The person who keeps the score
senses.definition: a person whose job is to write down the points scored during a game or the answers on a test
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛中记下得分，或在考试中批阅答卷的人
senses.example: The marker raised her flag as soon as the ball crossed the line.
senses.exampleCN: 球一过线，记分员就举起了旗子。
senses.why: The suffix -er can name a person as well as a thing, so a marker can be the one who makes the marks on a score sheet.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -er 既能指物也能指人，所以 marker 也可以指在记分表上做标记的那个人。

senses.title: Something that sets a purpose
senses.definition: in work and sport, a declared aim or initial achievement that later efforts must match
senses.definitionCN: 在工作与竞技中公开设定的目标，或先取得的成绩，作为后来者要赶超的基准
senses.example: By finishing the first race the young club put down a marker for the season.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻俱乐部跑完第一场比赛，就算给整个赛季立下了一根标杆。
senses.why: A stake in the ground shows how far one has come, and setting it out becomes a public promise of what will be reached.
senses.whyCN: 插在地上的标桩标出已经走到的位置，把它公开竖起来，就成了一种「将会达到哪里」的承诺。

senses.title: A dash in a text
senses.definition: in printing and typography, a short dash or similar sign used to divide or set off part of a printed line
senses.definitionCN: 在印刷与排版中用来分隔或标出文字段落的一条短横线或类似符号
senses.example: The old proofreader called the long dash a marker rather than a dash.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老校对把长横线叫作 marker，而不叫 dash。
senses.why: Printing needed a general word for any sign that marks a division, so the dash took the name of the tool that makes marks.
senses.whyCN: 印刷业需要一个泛称来指任何用来标示分隔的符号，于是短横线就借用了「做记号之物」的名字。

senses.title: A genetic sign on a strand
senses.definition: in biology, a gene or piece of DNA that can be traced and so identifies an individual, a breed or a trait
senses.definitionCN: 生物学上可追踪的一段基因或脱氧核糖核酸，用来识别个体、品种或某种性状
senses.example: The lab used a genetic marker to match the seedlings to their parent trees.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室用一段遗传标记把幼苗与它们的母树对应起来。
senses.why: Modern science puts the marker where no eye can look: a short stretch of DNA that marks which line a plant or animal came from.
senses.whyCN: 现代科学把标记放到了肉眼看不见的地方：一小段脱氧核糖核酸，用来标明动植物来自哪一血统。

intro.en: Marker is native English: an Old English noun mark plus the agent suffix -er, so it means literally the thing that marks.
intro.cn: marker 是英语本土的派生词：古英语名词 mark 加表示施事者的后缀 -er，字面意思是「做记号的东西」。

items.en: The Common Germanic noun is reconstructed as marko, meaning a boundary or a sign laid down to show a limit.
items.cn: 一般认为共同日耳曼语的名词重构为 marko，指边界，或为标示界限而设下的记号。

items.en: Old English mearc named a boundary, a landmark or a written sign; the idea of a dividing line is already there.
items.cn: 古英语 mearc 指边界、地标或书写的符号，其中已经包含「分界线」的观念。

items.en: The spelling settled on mark, and the verb mark grew beside the noun to mean putting such a sign on something.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 mark，名词旁又长出动词 mark，表示把这样的记号加在某物上。

items.en: Mark plus the suffix -er formed marker, first for a person who makes marks; the precise first date is uncertain.
items.cn: mark 加后缀 -er 构成 marker，最初指做标记的人；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The word widened from people to posts, pens, scores and genes, keeping the single idea of a sign that says where.
items.cn: 这个词从人扩展到标桩、笔、分数与基因，但始终保留一个观念：它是一个说出「在哪里」的标记。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same Germanic word for a boundary or a sign; the near-meaning group gathers other things that show a place or a level.
note.cn: 形近组收由同一个表示边界或记号的日耳曼词构成的词；近义组收其他用来标示位置或水平的词。

entries.definition: a sign, spot or line on a surface; also the verb to put such a sign on something
entries.definitionCN: 物体表面的痕迹、斑点或线条；也作动词，意为做记号。是 marker 的母词

entries.definition: clearly noticeable or standing out from the rest
entries.definitionCN: 明显可察觉的；突出的。由动词加 -ed 构成

entries.definition: a pattern of marks on an animal or object, or the scoring of a test
entries.definitionCN: 动物身上或物体上的斑纹，也指试卷评分

entries.definition: a board or notice that gives information or a direction
entries.definitionCN: 提供信息或指示方向的牌子或告示，比 marker 更强调它所写的文字

entries.definition: a building or feature that is easy to see and used to find the position of a traveller
entries.definitionCN: 显眼易认、可用来定位的建筑或景物，规模通常比 marker 大

entries.definition: a light or fire set high up to guide travellers or ships
entries.definitionCN: 设在高处用来指引旅人或船只的灯或火，常含发出的光，而 marker 只是一处静止的标记

normalIntro.en: These hooks build on the real Germanic root of mark and on the compounds the word actually forms.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子依据 mark 真实的日耳曼词根，以及这个词实际构成的复合词。

normal.en: Marker is simply mark plus -er, so it is the thing or person that marks.
normal.cn: marker 就是 mark 加 -er，也就是「做记号的东西或人」。

normal.en: Old English mearc meant a boundary, which is why a marker often stands at the edge of a field.
normal.cn: 古英语 mearc 意为边界，所以 marker 常常立在田地的边缘。

normal.en: A marker pen is named for its thick line, not for its tip; permanence means it will not rub off.
normal.cn: marker pen 因它画出的粗线而得名；permanent 表示不会擦掉。

normal.en: To put down a marker is to show publicly where you stand before others show theirs.
normal.cn: put down a marker 就是在别人表明位置之前，先公开亮出自己的位置。

normal.en: The same family runs from mark to marked and landmark, all about signs that say where.
normal.cn: 同一词族从 mark 延伸到 marked 与 landmark，都在讲「标明在哪里」的记号。

abstract.en: Picture a felt tip pressed to cardboard, ink spreading in a wide bright line, while the pen itself stays in the hand.
abstract.cn: 想象毡头压在纸板上，墨水晕开成一条鲜亮的宽线，而那支笔始终握在手里。

abstract.en: Now the pen is replaced by a painted post in tall grass: a small bright thing that stands where eyes look.
abstract.cn: 现在笔被换成长草里一根漆色的木桩：一个立在视线所及之处的小亮点。

abstract.en: Rise higher and the post becomes a line on a progress chart, separating what counts from what does not yet.
abstract.cn: 再升高一层，木桩变成进度图上的一条线，把算数和不还不算数的分开。

examples.en: The teacher drew a circle on the board with a red marker.
examples.cn: 老师用一支红色记号笔在黑板上画了一个圈。

examples.en: Stone markers line the footpath every hundred metres.
examples.cn: 沿途每隔一段路就立着一块界石。

examples.en: A rising birth rate is often taken as a marker of economic confidence.
examples.cn: 出生率上升常被看作是经济信心恢复的标志。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马可」——马克·波罗一路留下记号，后来这种笔就叫马克笔；这只是把音近的词凑在一起，与词源无关。

root: 共同日耳曼语 *marko「边界、分界记号」→ 古英语 mearc「边界、地标、符号」→ 中古英语 mark（名、动词）→ 英语加后缀 -er 构成 marker，字面义「做记号之物」。

sensesIntro.en: Marker is one job in many forms: a pen that marks, a post standing at a boundary, a score that fixes a level, a sign showing a process, a person keeping the score, an aim set down in public, a dash in print and a gene in science.
sensesIntro.cn: marker 是同一件事的多种形态：做记号的笔、立在边界的桩、划定水平的分数、显示进程的迹象、记分的人、公开立下的目标、印刷中的横线，以及科学中的基因。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a painted post standing at the edge of the field, saying where the line runs.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根漆色的木桩立在地边，说明边界在哪里。

branches.en: THE TOOL: the pen that makes marks, and the dash that marks a division in print.
branches.cn: 工具线：留下记号的笔，以及印刷中用来标示分隔的横线。

branches.en: THE PLACE: an object standing in a position to show where something is.
branches.cn: 位置线：立在某处、标示某物所在的物件。

branches.en: THE LEVEL: a line between pass and fail, and a visible sign of a hidden process.
branches.cn: 水平线：及格与不及格之间的那条线，以及隐藏进程外显的迹象。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the one who makes the marks on a score sheet.
branches.cn: 人物线：在记分表上做标记的那个人。

branches.en: THE PROMISE AND THE GENE: a public aim set as a stake, and a stretch of DNA that marks a line.
branches.cn: 两端的标记：立作标桩的公开目标，以及标出血统的一段基因。

intro.en: Marker is a plain English formation: a Germanic noun for a boundary mark plus the agent suffix -er, which English uses for both people and things.
intro.cn: marker 是朴素的英语构词：表示边界记号的名词加施事后缀 -er，这个后缀在英语里既可指人也可指物。

latinIntro.en: The word has no Latin ancestor; it is a native Germanic formation, so no Latin counterpart is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语祖先，是本土日耳曼语构词，因此不列拉丁同源词。

items.meaning: a boundary, a landmark, a sign
items.example: Mearc is the earliest recorded English form.
items.exampleCN: mearc 是最早有记录的英语形式。

items.meaning: a sign or spot on a surface
items.example: Mud prints left a mark on the carpet.
items.exampleCN: 泥脚印在地毯上留下了痕迹。

items.meaning: to put a sign on something
items.example: Mark the page before you close the book.
items.exampleCN: 合上书之前先给这一页做个记号。

items.example: The suffix -er turns the verb into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 把动词变成名词。

items.example: A marker showed where the path divided.
items.exampleCN: 一个标记标明小径在哪里分岔。

items.example: The ending -ed forms marked.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 marked。

items.example: Land is the first half of landmark.
items.exampleCN: land 是 landmark 的前半部分。

items.meaning: a feature used to find the position of a traveller
items.example: The tower is a landmark on the coast for ships in the bay.
items.exampleCN: 这座塔是湾内每艘船的地标。

items.example: The ending -ing forms marking.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 marking。

definition_zh: 旱獭；土拨鼠；隐入更深处的旧用法（a marmot 指深居简出的隐士）；坐等他人传递消息的人
definition_en: a small heavy ground squirrel with short legs and a loud warning call, common in the mountains of Europe, Asia and North America
core_image: 高山草坡上，一只圆胖的棕灰色旱獭用后腿立起，前爪收在胸前，警惕地望向远方
scene: 高原的草坡上，一群旱獭正在洞口翻晒身体，忽然一只发出尖锐的叫声，整群立刻钻回地下。When one marmot gives its warning whistle, the whole colony vanishes into the burrows.
sceneCN: 这里 marmot 是「旱獭」（第 1 个义项：生活在高山草甸的粗壮地松鼠）；句意：一只旱獭发出警示的尖哨，整个群体就钻进洞穴不见了。图中可辨认的事物有洞口、草坡与远处积雪的山脊。

pos.zh: 旱獭；土拨鼠（高山草地上的大型地松鼠）

collocations.zh: 高山旱獭（阿尔卑斯山区常见的那种）
黄腹旱獭（北美落基山区常见）

derivatives.zh: 由本词经拉丁化构成的属名，指旱獭属，如 Marmota marmota 为高山旱獭
由本词加 -like 构成，义为「像旱獭一样的」，常形容体型圆胖、爱钻洞的动物或人
由属名加 -ine 构成的旧式形容词，义为「旱獭的」，多见于旧时博物学文献

senses.title: The heavy mountain ground squirrel
senses.definition: a large stocky rodent of the ground squirrel family that lives in mountain meadows and sleeps through the long cold season
senses.definitionCN: 地松鼠科的大型粗壮啮齿动物，栖息在高山草甸，以冬眠度过漫长寒季
senses.example: A marmot sat upright on a rock, watching the hikers cross the pass.
senses.exampleCN: 一只旱獭直立在岩石上，看着徒步者翻过山口。
senses.why: The animal itself is the earliest and central sense; every other sense of the word grows out of the mountain creature and its habits.
senses.whyCN: 动物本身才是最古老、最核心的义项；这个词的其他义项都由这种高山动物及其习性延伸而来。

senses.title: The forest creature of Swiss legend
senses.titleCN: 瑞士传说中的森林小兽
senses.definition: in Swiss folklore, a small lively animal that figures in jesting tales and patriotic songs of the mountain cantons
senses.definitionCN: 瑞士民间传说中一种活泼的小兽，常出现在山区的玩笑故事与爱国歌曲里
senses.example: The old song calls the forest marmot a cheerful little companion of shepherds.
senses.exampleCN: 那首老歌把森林里的小旱獭称作牧羊人快活的伙伴。
senses.why: Alpine language used the name for small beasts found in the woods as well, and legend gathered around them until the word carried a folkloric tint.
senses.whyCN: 阿尔卑斯山区的说法也把林子里的小兽叫作这个名字，传说再围绕它们积累起来，于是词义带上了一层民间故事的色彩。

senses.title: The habit of sleeping away the winter
senses.definition: used, especially with like, for a long deep sleep or a hasty retreat underground when danger threatens
senses.definitionCN: 常与 like 连用，指漫长深沉的睡眠，也指遇到危险时匆忙钻入地下的躲避行为
senses.example: During the coldest weeks the village sleeps like a marmot behind its snowed-in windows.
senses.exampleCN: 最冷的几周里，村庄就像旱獭一样，在积雪封住的窗后沉沉睡去。
senses.why: A hibernating marmot is the most familiar picture of winter sleep, so comparisons transfer the habit from the animal to people.
senses.whyCN: 冬眠中的旱獭是冬天睡觉最熟悉的画面，于是人们用比较的方式把它这个习性挪到人身上。

senses.title: A watchful animal giving a warning
senses.definition: used of a group in which one member is posted as a lookout and sounds a call when danger appears
senses.definitionCN: 用于形容有成员被放哨、遇到危险便发出叫声的群体
senses.example: One old marmot always keeps watch on the highest rock and calls the alarm for the colony.
senses.exampleCN: 总有一只年老旱獭蹲在最高的石头上，为整个群体放哨报警。
senses.why: Marmot colonies really do post sentries and whistle at danger, so the word can stand for the whole pattern of group watchfulness.
senses.whyCN: 旱獭群落确实会设岗放哨、遇险时发出哨声，因此这个词也可以代表整套群体警戒的行为模式。

senses.title: The short-lived word for a hermit
senses.titleCN: 旧语中的隐士；深居之人
senses.definition: an obsolete use of the name to mean a hermit or recluse, with the implication of living hidden away like a burrow dweller
senses.definitionCN: 这个词的旧用法，指隐士或深居简出的人，隐含像钻洞的动物一样藏起来生活的意味
senses.example: The seventeenth-century letter writer was a marmot, shut in his library for the whole winter.
senses.exampleCN: 那位十七世纪的书信作者是个隐士，整个冬天都关在书房里。
senses.why: A word that once meant the burrow dweller could be turned on people who hide in their own burrows, a use that later faded.
senses.whyCN: 一个本来指钻洞动物的词，可以被拿来说那些把自己藏进「洞穴」里生活的人，这种用法后来逐渐消失。

intro.en: Marmot reached French and English from the Alpine dialects of the Alps; its link to Latin muris montis, mouse of the mountains, is a later folk explanation rather than the actual source.
intro.cn: marmot 从阿尔卑斯山区的方言进入法语与英语；把它说成来自拉丁语 muris montis（山里的老鼠），是后起的民间解释，并非真实来源。

items.en: The creature name in the Alps is generally taken to be a Romance word of the Alps, though its exact origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 阿尔卑斯山区对它的称呼一般认为是当地罗曼语的说法，但确切的来源不确定。

items.en: French recorded the word with a final t, which later fell silent in the spoken form.
