items.cn: 法语记录到这个名词时带着词尾的 t，后来在口语里这个 t 不再发音。

items.en: English borrowed the word through French naturalists and keeps the spelling, though the final letter is not pronounced.
items.cn: 英语经法国博物学者借入这个词，保留了拼写，只是词尾字母不发音。

items.en: Many sources explain the word as muris montis, mouse of the mountains, which fits the French spelling but is now treated as a guess.
items.cn: 许多资料把它解释为 muris montis（山里的老鼠），与法语拼写恰好吻合，如今被视为推测而非词源。

items.en: Zoology fixed the word on the stocky alpine rodent, and the old hermit sense dropped away.
items.cn: 动物学把这个词固定用在体型粗壮的阿尔卑斯山区啮齿动物身上，旧的隐士义也随之消失。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that rhyme or look close to marmot; the near-meaning group gathers other small mammals people often confuse with it.
note.cn: 形近组收与 marmot 押韵或外形相近的词；近义组收常被与它混淆的其他小型哺乳动物。

entries.definition: the Latin genus name for the marmots, from which the English creature name was taken
entries.definitionCN: 旱獭属的拉丁属名，英语的动物名正取自它

entries.definition: an old dialectal form of marble; it just looks like marmot but comes from another root
entries.definitionCN: marble 的一种旧方言拼法，只是看起来像 marmot，词源不同

entries.definition: an old Russian form of mammoth; its shape is close to marmot but it names a giant elephant
entries.definitionCN: mammoth 的旧俄语形式，外形与 marmot 相近，但指的是一头巨象，词源不同

entries.definition: a North American marmot of the eastern states, famous for its shadow on a February day
entries.definitionCN: 美国东部的一种旱獭，因二月的影子传说而闻名，是 marmot 的一种

entries.definition: a small burrowing rodent of the North American plains that stands up and yaps at danger
entries.definitionCN: 北美草原上一种会挖洞的小型啮齿动物，遇险时会立起身来吠叫，体型比旱獭小

entries.definition: a burrowing rodent of North America, variously a pocket gopher or a ground squirrel near the surface
entries.definitionCN: 北美多种穴居啮齿动物的通称，可为囊鼠或浅层地松鼠，与旱獭都有钻洞习性

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the real Alpine origin and the words the animal actually forms in English.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子依据它真实的阿尔卑斯方言来源，以及这种动物在英语里实际构成的词。

normal.en: Marmot came to English from the Alps through French, and the final letter is still silent.
normal.cn: marmot 经法语从阿尔卑斯山区进入英语，词尾那个字母至今不发音。

normal.en: The Latin explanation of mouse of the mountains fits the letters but is only a later guess.
normal.cn: 「山里的老鼠」这一拉丁语解释与拼写吻合，却只是后来的推测。

normal.en: The genus name Marmota is the same creature, only dressed in scientific Latin.
normal.cn: 属名 Marmota 指的是同一种动物，只是披上了科学拉丁语的外衣。

normal.en: A yellow-bellied marmot and an alpine marmot are cousins: one in the Rockies, one in Europe.
normal.cn: 黄腹旱獭与高山旱獭是近亲：一个在落基山，一个在欧洲。

normal.en: A groundhog is a marmot by another name, which is why the shadow story is about a marmot.
normal.cn: groundhog 其实就是旱獭的另一种叫法，所以那个关于影子的故事说的正是旱獭。

abstract.en: Picture a round grey-brown body on a green slope, sitting up like a small person with paws folded.
abstract.cn: 想象绿色山坡上一个圆滚滚的棕灰身影，像小人一样坐直，前爪收在胸前。

abstract.en: Then the slope is a village square, and the little creature has become a character in a song of the mountains.
abstract.cn: 再把山坡换成村庄的广场，这只小兽就成了山区歌谣里的一个角色。

abstract.en: Winter comes, snow covers the slope, and one by one the grey bodies drop into the dark burrows to sleep.
abstract.cn: 冬天来了，雪盖住山坡，那些灰色的身影一个接一个钻进黑洞里睡去。

examples.en: Marmots dig deep burrows in which several families spend the whole winter.
examples.cn: 旱獭挖出很深的洞穴，几个家庭在那里度过整个冬天。

examples.en: Visitors are told not to feed the marmots near the mountain road.
examples.cn: 游客被告知不要喂食山路旁的旱獭。

examples.en: The alpine marmot survives cold nights by huddling with others in its burrow.
examples.cn: 高山旱獭靠与其他同类在洞里挤在一起，熬过寒冷的夜晚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「妈默特」——妈妈特地叮嘱别去掏洞，洞里有会打哨的胖家伙；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 阿尔卑斯山区的罗曼语方言对旱獭的称呼，一般认为由该方言进入法语，再经博物学研究带入英语，词尾字母不发音；确切来源不确定。以拉丁语 muris montis「山里的老鼠」解释，是后起的民间说法。

sensesIntro.en: Marmot begins with the stocky mountain animal, passes through its folklore and its habits of winter sleep and sentry duty, and ends with an old hermit sense that has faded.
sensesIntro.cn: marmot 从体型粗壮的高山动物出发，经由瑞士传说中的形象与它冬眠、放哨的习性，最后落到一个已经消失的「隐士」旧义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a round brown-grey animal sitting upright at its burrow, looking out over the high meadow.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只圆胖的棕灰色旱獭在洞口直立起身，望向高山草甸。

branches.en: THE ANIMAL: the stocky burrowing rodent is the literal and central sense.
branches.cn: 动物线：这种粗壮会挖洞的啮齿动物是字面义与核心义。

branches.en: THE STORY: Swiss song and legend take the small creature into folklore.
branches.cn: 传说线：瑞士的歌谣与传说把这种小兽带进了民间故事。

branches.en: THE HABITS: winter sleep in the burrow and a watchful sentry with its whistle.
branches.cn: 习性线：洞中过冬的沉睡，以及放哨者发出的警报哨声。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: a burrow dweller of an old usage stands for a hermit.
branches.cn: 比喻线：旧用法里那个钻洞的小东西，被用来比喻深居简出的隐士。

branches.en: THE COMPARISON: mountain people say others sleep like a marmot through the cold weeks.
branches.cn: 类比线：山区的人说别人像旱獭一样睡过整个寒季。

intro.en: Marmot has no English parts: it is a borrowed Alpine name, and English only builds Latinized and fancy forms around it.
intro.cn: marmot 没有多少英语构件：它是借来的阿尔卑斯名字，英语只在它周围造出拉丁化的形式与文气的说法。

latinIntro.en: Latin gives the word only its scientific genus name and a linking adjective; the creature name itself is not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语只给了这个词一个科学属名与一个连接形容词，动物名本身并不来自拉丁语。

items.example: A marmot whistled from the slope.
items.exampleCN: 一只旱獭在坡上叫了一声。

items.example: The marmots share one system of burrows.
items.exampleCN: 这些旱獭共用同一套洞穴。

items.meaning: kept from the French spelling but not pronounced
items.meaningCN: 保留自法语的词尾字母，不发音
items.example: The final -t is silent, as in other French borrowings.
items.exampleCN: 词尾的 -t 不发音，与其他法语借词一样。

items.example: Naturalists put the animal in the genus Marmota.
items.exampleCN: 博物学者把这种动物归入旱獭属。

items.meaning: the ordinary ending of many Latin genus names
items.meaningCN: 许多拉丁属名的阴性词尾
items.example: The ending -a makes the genus name feminine.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -a 使属名成为阴性。

items.meaning: belonging to, of the nature of
items.example: The suffix -ine forms the old adjective marmotine.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ine 构成旧式形容词 marmotine。

items.example: The suffix -like forms marmot-like.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -like 构成 marmot-like。

items.example: A groundhog is one kind of marmot.
items.exampleCN: groundhog 是旱獭的一种。

items.meaning: a tunnel dug by an animal for shelter
items.example: The marmot sleeps in a deep burrow.
items.exampleCN: 旱獭睡在深深的洞穴里。

definition_zh: 有袋类动物；有袋目动物
definition_en: a mammal whose young are carried in a pouch on the mother body after birth
core_image: 幼崽爬进母亲腹前的育儿袋，探出小脑袋
scene: 凌晨的桉树林里，一只母袋鼠肚子上的育儿袋露出一只小袋鼠的耳朵。A joey poked its head out of the pouch of a grazing marsupial.
sceneCN: 这里 marsupial 是「有袋类动物」（第 1 个义项：用育儿袋哺养幼崽的哺乳动物）；句意：小袋鼠把头从一个正在吃草的有袋动物育儿袋里探了出来。

pos.zh: 有袋类动物；有袋目动物

collocations.zh: 澳大利亚的有袋类动物

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词直接借入，指育儿袋或阴囊
加 -ization 构成，医学上指把囊肿壁缝开形成袋状引流口
加 -ian 构成的形容词，指与有袋类有关的

senses.title: A pouched mammal
senses.definition: a mammal such as a kangaroo or koala whose young are carried in a pouch after a short pregnancy
senses.definitionCN: 袋鼠、考拉这类哺乳动物，妊娠期很短，幼崽出生后藏在育儿袋里继续发育
senses.example: Kangaroos and koalas are marsupials.
senses.exampleCN: 袋鼠和考拉都是有袋类动物。
senses.why: The Latin word for pouch became the name of the whole group, because the pouch is what sets them apart from other mammals.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语里「小袋」这个词后来成了整类动物的名字，因为育儿袋正是它们区别于其他哺乳动物的标志。

senses.title: The pouched order
senses.definition: the taxonomic group of mammals that includes kangaroos, koalas, opossums, and their relatives
senses.definitionCN: 动物分类中有袋目的统称，包括袋鼠、考拉、负鼠及其近亲
senses.example: The marsupial is one of the major mammal groups.
senses.exampleCN: 有袋目是哺乳动物的几个主要类群之一。
senses.why: Biology turned the descriptive word into a formal category, so the noun can name the order rather than a single animal.
senses.whyCN: 生物学把这个描述性的词提升为正式分类名，因此名词也可以指整个有袋目，而不只是某一种动物。

senses.title: Of pouched mammals
senses.definition: relating to or belonging to the pouched mammals
senses.definitionCN: 与有袋类哺乳动物有关的，或属于这一类的
senses.example: The marsupial lineage split from other mammals long ago.
senses.exampleCN: 有袋类的进化支系在很久以前就与其他哺乳动物分离了。
senses.why: English often uses the same form as an adjective, so the word can describe a lineage or a feature instead of naming an animal.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用同一个词形作形容词，于是它可以描述一个进化支系或一种特征，而不只是指某只动物。

intro.en: Marsupial comes from Latin marsupium, a pouch, which comes from Greek marsipos, meaning bag; the biological sense for pouched mammals is a modern coinage.
intro.cn: marsupial 来自拉丁语 marsupium（小袋），后者又源于希腊语 marsipos（袋子）；「有袋类哺乳动物」这个生物学义项是近代才有的。

items.en: Marsipos means a bag or pouch, recorded as a word for a small sack.
items.cn: 古希腊语 marsipos 意为袋子、小口袋。

items.en: The Latin borrowing marsupium names a purse or pouch.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入该词，写作 marsupium，指钱袋或小袋。

items.en: In medical Latin marsupium also names the scrotal sac.
items.cn: 在医学拉丁语中，marsupium 也用来指阴囊。

items.en: The adjective marsupial appears first for purse-like anatomical structures.
items.cn: 英语中 marsupial 先作为形容词出现，用于描述类似口袋的解剖结构。

items.en: Naturalists apply the word to kangaroos and opossums, and the noun names the group.
items.cn: 博物学家把这个词用于袋鼠、负鼠等动物，名词义「有袋类」由此确立。

note.en: Marsupial is the bag word, close in form to marsupium, and in meaning to mammal, monotreme, and placental.
note.cn: marsupial 本义与「袋子」相关，形式上接近 marsupium，语义上与 mammal、monotreme、placental 这类哺乳动物分类词相邻。

entries.definition: the pouch of a marsupial
entries.definitionCN: 育儿袋；同为「袋子」词根

entries.definition: formed into or treated with a pouch, in surgery
entries.definitionCN: 外科上缝成袋状的，由同一词根加动词后缀而来

entries.definition: a rare old name for a pouched gill fish
entries.definitionCN: 旧时一种鱼类名，同取希腊语「袋子」词根

entries.definition: a warm-blooded animal that feeds its young with milk
entries.definitionCN: 哺乳动物，有袋类属于其中一支

entries.definition: an egg-laying mammal such as the platypus
entries.definitionCN: 单孔类动物，如鸭嘴兽，是另一支特殊哺乳动物

entries.definition: belonging to the mammals whose young develop in a womb with a placenta
entries.definitionCN: 有胎盘类哺乳动物的，与有袋类相对

normalIntro.en: Marsupial is built on the Latin word for a pouch, so the whole word is a labelled bag.
normalIntro.cn: marsupial 建立在拉丁语「小袋」这个词上，整个词本身就像一只标着名字的袋子。

normal.en: The -ium in marsupium is a Latin noun ending for a thing, like a container.
normal.cn: marsupium 里的 -ium 是拉丁语名词词尾，常指某样物件，像容器。

normal.en: Keep marsupial next to pouch: the word and the feature were born together.
normal.cn: 把 marsupial 和 pouch 放在一起记：这个词和这个特征是一起诞生的。

normal.en: The plural marsupials is regular, just add -s.
normal.cn: 复数 marsupials 变化规则，直接加 -s。

normal.en: As an adjective, marsupial stands before nouns such as lineage or pouch.
normal.cn: 作形容词时，marsupial 放在 lineage、pouch 这类名词前面。

normal.en: Compare monotreme and placental, the other two big mammal branches.
normal.cn: 对比 monotreme 和 placental，那是哺乳动物的另外两大分支。

abstract.en: Picture a joey climbing into a bag and peeking out.
abstract.cn: 想象一只小袋鼠爬进袋子里又探出头来。

abstract.en: Draw a cupboard full of pouches, each with a label on the strap.
abstract.cn: 想象一只装满小袋的柜子，每个袋子的带子上都挂着名字。

abstract.en: Imagine a branch of animals carrying their babies in front pockets.
abstract.cn: 想象树上的一个动物分支，个个都把宝宝揣在胸前口袋。

examples.en: The zoo keeps several marsupials from Australia.
examples.cn: 动物园养着几只有袋类动物，来自澳大利亚。

examples.en: A marsupial carries its newborn in a pouch until it grows stronger.
examples.cn: 有袋类动物把刚出生的幼崽放在育儿袋里，直到它长得更强壮。

examples.en: Ecologists study how drought affects marsupial populations.
examples.cn: 生态学家研究干旱如何影响有袋类种群。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「妈袋皮」——妈妈的皮袋子，就是育儿袋；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古希腊语 marsipos（袋子）→ 拉丁语 marsupium（小袋；医学中指阴囊）→ 英语 marsupial，核心义「带口袋的」。

sensesIntro.en: Marsupial starts as a name for animals that carry young in a pouch, then becomes a formal order in zoology, and finally works as an adjective.
sensesIntro.cn: marsupial 先指把幼崽装在育儿袋里的动物，再成为动物学中的正式目名，最后可作形容词使用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tiny joey safe inside its mother pouch.
core.cn: 核心意象：幼崽安安稳稳地待在母亲的育儿袋里。

branches.en: The animal itself is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 这只动物本身就是日常最常用的义项。

branches.en: The group label comes from biology.
branches.cn: 类群名称来自生物分类学。

branches.en: The adjective sense describes the lineage.
branches.cn: 形容词义用来修饰整个进化支系。

branches.en: One animal belongs to the larger order of pouch carriers.
branches.cn: 一种动物从属于更大的「带袋者」类群。

branches.en: A pouched animal and a pouched lineage share the same image.
branches.cn: 有袋动物与有袋支系共享同一个口袋意象。

intro.en: Marsupial grows from a Greek bag word into Latin then English, with marsupium and other technical words in the family.
intro.cn: marsupial 从一个希腊语「袋子」词经拉丁语进入英语，词族中还有 marsupium 等技术词。

latinIntro.en: Latin marsupium means a pouch or purse, borrowed from Greek marsipos.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 marsupium 意为小袋、钱袋，借自希腊语 marsipos。

items.example: Marsipos is the earliest form of the bag image.
items.exampleCN: marsipos 是「袋子」意象最早的词形。

items.example: Marsupium is the direct source of the word.
items.exampleCN: marsupium 是这个词的直接来源。

items.example: The suffix -al turns the pouch noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 把「袋子」这个名词变成形容词。

items.example: Marsupial names the whole group.
items.exampleCN: marsupial 指整个类群。

items.example: The adjective describes a feature or a lineage.
items.exampleCN: 形容词义描述特征或支系。

items.example: The plural adds a simple -s.
items.exampleCN: 复数只加一个 -s。

items.example: Marsupium names the pouch itself.
items.exampleCN: marsupium 指育儿袋本身。

items.meaningCN: 把……做成某种状态的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ization forms marsupialization.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ization 构成 marsupialization。

items.meaning: the surgical forming of a pouch
items.example: Marsupialization keeps a medical sense of the pouch.
items.exampleCN: marsupialization 保留了「袋子」的医学含义。

definition_zh: 战争的；军事的；尚武的
definition_en: relating to war, soldiers, or fighting, as in martial law or martial arts
core_image: 比武场上士兵举起长剑，号角声压过人群的嘈杂
scene: 古城墙上贴出告示，全城进入战时法令管制的状态。The governor declared martial law after the riots spread across the city.
sceneCN: 这里 martial 是「军事的、战争状态的」（第 2 个义项：与军队和战时管理有关的）；句意：骚乱蔓延全城后，总督宣布实施军事管制法。

derivatives.zh: 由 -ism 构成，指尚武精神或军事主义
由 -ly 构成，义为「以军事方式；威武地」
由 -ness 构成，指尚武、好战的性质

senses.title: Connected with war
senses.definition: connected with or suitable for war and armed fighting
senses.definitionCN: 与战争、武装战斗有关或适合战场的
senses.example: The poem celebrates a martial victory.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗歌颂一场战争的胜利。
senses.why: The name of Mars, the Roman god of war, gave the adjective its meaning, so anything warlike became martial.
senses.whyCN: 罗马战神马尔斯的名字给了这个形容词含义，因此凡是像战争的东西都叫 martial。

senses.title: Under army control
senses.definition: used of rules or measures imposed by the army in place of civil government
senses.definitionCN: 指军队代替民政当局强行推行的规则或措施
senses.example: The city stayed under martial rule for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市受军事管制达一周。
senses.why: When the army takes over law and order, its rules are called martial because the war god is now in charge.
senses.whyCN: 当军队接管治安时，它的规则被称为 martial，因为这时当家的是「战神」。

senses.title: Of fighting skills
senses.definition: relating to combat sports and self-defence systems such as judo, karate, and kung fu
senses.definitionCN: 指柔道、空手道、功夫等格斗运动和自卫技法
senses.example: She has trained in martial arts since childhood.
senses.exampleCN: 她从小就练习武术。
senses.why: Fighting arts were named after the war god, so modern self-defence sports keep the same name.
senses.whyCN: 格斗技艺曾以战神来命名，所以现代的自卫运动也沿用了这个称呼。

senses.title: Warlike in spirit
senses.definition: describing a person, people, or mood that is eager for war or fond of fighting
senses.definitionCN: 形容人或民族、情绪热衷于战争或好斗
senses.example: His martial temper frightened the neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 他好斗的脾气把邻居吓坏了。
senses.why: The adjective moved from talk about warfare to talk about the warriors themselves, describing their temper.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从描述战争本身，扩展到描述战士的性格，于是用来形容好战的脾气。

intro.en: Martial comes from Latin martialis, of Mars, the Roman god of war; Mars itself is generally linked to an older Italic root for a powerful force.
intro.cn: martial 来自拉丁语 martialis，意为「属马尔斯的」，马尔斯是罗马神话中的战神；Mars 一般认为源于更早的意大利语族词根，表示强大的力量。

items.en: Reconstructed forms suggest that Mars was felt as a force rather than a person.
items.cn: 据重构形式推测，早期的 Mars 更接近一种力量，而不是一个人格化的神。

items.en: Mars is the Roman god of war, and the month of March is named after him.
items.cn: Mars 是罗马战神，三月 Mars 也以他命名。

items.en: The adjective martialis means belonging to Mars.
items.cn: 形容词 martialis 意为「属于马尔斯的」。

items.en: French martial carries the adjective forward.
items.cn: 古法语 martial 把这一形容词继续传下来。

items.en: English martial appears first for things of war and later for fighting arts.
items.cn: 英语 martial 最早指与战争有关的事物，后来也用于格斗技艺。

note.en: Martial is the Mars adjective, sharing a form with the name March and meaning with military, warlike, and combative.
note.cn: martial 是「马尔斯」的形容词，形式上与月份词 March 相近，意义上与 military、warlike、combative 相邻。

entries.definition: the Roman god of war
entries.definitionCN: 罗马战神马尔斯，martial 的来源

entries.definition: the third month, named after Mars
entries.definitionCN: 三月，以战神命名，与 martial 同源

entries.definition: in a warlike or military way
entries.definitionCN: 以军事或尚武的方式，是加 -ly 的副词

entries.definition: relating to armed forces or soldiers
entries.definitionCN: 军队的；军事的，比 martial 更中性

entries.definition: eager to fight or start wars
entries.definitionCN: 好战的；战争般的

entries.definition: ready to argue or fight
entries.definitionCN: 好斗的，多用于形容性格

normalIntro.en: Martial is simply the adjective of Mars, so every phrase with it has a sword in the background.
normalIntro.cn: martial 就是「马尔斯」的形容词，所以每个含它的短语背后都有一把剑。

normal.en: Mars, March, and martial form a small family.
normal.cn: Mars、March、martial 组成一个小词族。

normal.en: Martial law is what the army declares when civil order fails.
normal.cn: martial law 是军队在民政秩序失控时宣布的军事管制。

normal.en: Martial arts is the standard phrase for fighting sports.
normal.cn: martial arts 是格斗运动的固定说法。

normal.en: Do not confuse martial with marshal, the officer rank.
normal.cn: 不要与 marshal（元帅、警官的职衔）混淆。

normal.en: Martial belongs to writing about war and soldiers, not to everyday combat.
normal.cn: martial 多出现在写战争和军人的语境里，而不是日常打架。

abstract.en: Picture a battlefield where music and banners set the mood.
abstract.cn: 想象一个战场，军乐和旗帜定下了气氛。

abstract.en: Imagine a city sealed by soldiers and a notice on the gate.
abstract.cn: 想象一座被士兵封锁的城市，城门上贴着告示。

abstract.en: Picture hands wrapped in cloth bowing before a fight.
abstract.cn: 想象缠着布带的手在比试前抱拳行礼。

examples.en: Martial law was declared after the earthquake.
examples.cn: 地震后宣布实施军事管制法。

examples.en: The old temple still shows a martial spirit in its carved guards.
examples.cn: 这座古庙门前的石雕卫士仍显出尚武之气。

examples.en: She teaches martial arts to children on weekends.
examples.cn: 她周末教孩子们武术。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马术」——骑马作战的「马术」听起来像 martial，与战争、马有关；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 Mars（战神马尔斯）→ martialis（马尔斯的）→ 古法语 martial → 英语 martial，核心义「战神带来的、战争般的」。

sensesIntro.en: Martial starts with the god of war, covers war and army control, then reaches fighting skills and the warlike temper of people.
sensesIntro.cn: martial 从战神讲起，先是战争与军队管制，再延伸到格斗技艺和人的尚武脾气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a banner of the war god flying over a field of soldiers.
core.cn: 核心意象：战神的旗帜在士兵队列上空飘动。

branches.en: War itself is the earliest sense.
branches.cn: 战争本身是最早的义项。

branches.en: Army rule is war brought into ordinary life.
branches.cn: 军事管制是战争进入日常生活。

branches.en: Fighting arts borrow the war god name.
branches.cn: 格斗技艺借用了战神的名字。

branches.en: Warlike temper is war moved into the person.
branches.cn: 尚武脾气是战争从战场移入人的性格。

branches.en: Both martial law and martial arts keep strict discipline.
branches.cn: 军事管制法与武术都讲究严格的纪律。

intro.en: Martial is a loan adjective from Latin, with a small English family built by adding -ism, -ly, and -ness.
intro.cn: martial 是从拉丁语借来的形容词，英语用 -ism、-ly、-ness 等词尾建起了一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin martialis means of Mars, the god of war; the stem is the god name itself.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 martialis 意为「马尔斯的」，词干正是战神的名字。

items.example: Mars is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: Mars 是整个词族的基础。

items.example: Martialis gives the English adjective directly.
items.exampleCN: martialis 直接演变成英语形容词。

items.example: The suffix -al makes an adjective from the name.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 把神名变成形容词。

items.example: Martial describes war and army matters.
items.exampleCN: martial 描述战争与军队事务。

items.example: The suffix -ism forms martialism.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ism 构成 martialism。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms martially.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 martially。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms martialness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 martialness。

items.meaning: the third month, named after Mars
items.example: March shares the same god name.
items.exampleCN: March 与 martial 同取战神之名。

items.example: Marshal is only spelled like martial, with a different origin.
items.exampleCN: marshal 只是拼写相近，来源不同。

definition_zh: 奇迹；令人惊叹的事物；对……感到惊奇
definition_en: a wonderful thing that surprises you, or to feel great surprise and admiration
core_image: 抬起头睁大眼睛，被眼前的东西惊得说不出话
scene: 清晨的山谷里，游客第一次看到整片云海翻涌，久久说不出话。We marvelled at the colours of the sunset over the lake.
sceneCN: 这里 marvel 是动词「惊叹、对……感到惊奇」（第 3 个义项：因好奇或敬佩而感到惊讶）；句意：我们惊叹于湖上日落的色彩。

derivatives.zh: 由 -ous 构成，义为「奇妙的、极好的」
美式拼写的同形词，义为「奇妙的、了不起的」
由 -ly 构成，义为「奇妙地、极好地」

senses.title: A wonderful thing
senses.definition: something so unusual and impressive that it makes people wonder
senses.definitionCN: 异常罕见、令人印象深刻、让人惊叹的事物
senses.example: The bridge is a marvel of modern engineering.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥是现代工程的奇迹。
senses.why: The word began as the feeling of wonder, and was then applied to the thing that caused it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指惊叹的感觉，后来转指引起惊叹的那个东西。

senses.title: An amazing person
senses.definition: a person whose skill or character fills others with admiration
senses.definitionCN: 技艺或品格令人钦佩不已的人
senses.example: Grandmother was a marvel at ninety.
senses.exampleCN: 祖母九十岁时依然是个了不起的人。
senses.why: Because the noun can name anything that amazes, it also praises people in a warm, familiar way.
senses.whyCN: 既然名词可以指任何令人惊叹的事物，它自然也能以亲切口吻称赞某个人。

senses.title: To be amazed
senses.definition: to feel surprise and admiration at something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物感到惊讶和钦佩
senses.example: Visitors never cease to marvel at the canyon.
senses.exampleCN: 游客们总是惊叹于这座峡谷。
senses.why: The original verb meant to wonder, so the modern verb is the feeling itself acted out.
senses.whyCN: 古英语动词本义就是感到疑惑与惊奇，现代动词正是这种感受本身的动作化。

senses.title: Something wonderful in a book
senses.definition: a wondrous thing met in a story, myth, or travel account
senses.definitionCN: 在故事、神话或游记中遇到的奇物奇景
senses.example: The old travel book is full of marvels.
senses.exampleCN: 那本古旧游记里满是奇观。
senses.why: Readers of myths and voyages took the word for the strange creatures and places such tales describe.
senses.whyCN: 神话和游记的读者用这个词指书中描述的那些奇异生物与地方。

intro.en: Marvel comes from Old French merveille, from Latin mirabilia, wonderful things, which grew from the verb mirari, to wonder.
intro.cn: marvel 来自古法语 merveille，上溯至拉丁语 mirabilia（奇妙之事），根源是动词 mirari（惊叹、疑惑）。

items.en: The verb mirari means to wonder at, and its adjective mirabilis means wonderful.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 mirari 意为惊叹、感到疑惑，其形容词 mirabilis 意为奇妙的。

items.en: The plural noun mirabilia names miraculous or wonderful things.
items.cn: 复数名词 mirabilia 指神迹、奇妙之事。

items.en: The word becomes merveille, meaning a wonder or miracle.
items.cn: 这一词形在古法语中变为 merveille，意为惊奇、奇迹。

items.en: Middle English adopts the word as merveil or marvel.
items.cn: 中古英语以 merveil 或 marvel 的形式借用它。

items.en: The noun settles as marvel, and the verb comes to mean to be amazed.
items.cn: 现代英语中名词定型为 marvel，动词则表示惊叹、感到惊奇。

note.en: Marvel carries the wonder root shared with miracle and marvellous, and sits beside wonder, miracle, and admire.
note.cn: marvel 带着与 miracle、marvellous 共享的「惊奇」词根，语义上与 wonder、miracle、admire 相邻。

entries.definition: extremely good or wonderful
entries.definitionCN: 奇妙的；极好的，是加 -ous 的形容词

entries.definition: wonderful things, marvellous curiosities
entries.definitionCN: 奇妙之事；奇珍，同取拉丁语「惊奇」词根

entries.definition: an extraordinary event believed to come from a higher power
entries.definitionCN: 神迹；奇迹，与 marvel 同源于拉丁语 mirari

entries.definition: a strange and beautiful thing, or the feeling it creates
entries.definitionCN: 奇观；惊奇之感，是最贴近的同义词

entries.definition: an amazing event beyond ordinary explanation
entries.definitionCN: 超越常理解释的奇迹，语气比 marvel 更强

entries.definition: to respect and approve of something with pleasure
entries.definitionCN: 钦佩；赞美，侧重欣赏而非惊讶

normalIntro.en: Marvel is the wonder word: it names the feeling of surprise and the thing that causes it.
normalIntro.cn: marvel 是表示「惊奇」的词：既指惊讶的感受，也指引起这种感受的东西。

normal.en: Marvel at is the usual verb pattern.
normal.cn: marvel at 是动词最常用的搭配模式。

normal.en: The adjective is marvellous, not marvel.
normal.cn: 对应的形容词是 marvellous，而不是 marvel。

normal.en: British spelling doubles the L, American spelling uses one L.
normal.cn: 英式拼写双写 L，美式拼写只写一个 L。

normal.en: The plural marvels means wonders or amazing things.
normal.cn: 复数 marvels 指多个奇观或奇妙的事物。

normal.en: Compare wonder, which is the closer everyday synonym.
normal.cn: 对比 wonder，那是更贴近的日常同义词。

abstract.en: Picture a child stopping to stare at a huge waterfall.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子停下脚步，呆呆望着巨大的瀑布。

abstract.en: Think of a museum case of strange and beautiful objects.
abstract.cn: 想象博物馆展柜里那些奇异又美丽的物件。

abstract.en: Imagine a crowd gasping together at the night sky.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人对着夜空一起发出惊叹。

examples.en: The bridge is a marvel of modern engineering.
examples.cn: 这座桥是现代工程的奇迹。

examples.en: Tourists marvel at the size of the old tree.
examples.cn: 游客们惊叹于这棵古树的巨大。

examples.en: Ancient travelers returned home with tales of marvels.
examples.cn: 古代旅人回到家时带回了关于奇观的故事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「妈哦」——看到奇观时脱口而出的那声惊叹；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 mirari（惊叹、感到疑惑）→ mirabilia（奇妙之事）→ 古法语 merveille（惊奇；奇迹）→ 英语 marvel，核心义「让人惊得睁大眼睛」。

sensesIntro.en: Marvel first names a wonderful thing, then an amazing person, then the act of being amazed, and finally the strange things found in stories.
sensesIntro.cn: marvel 先指奇妙的事物，再指了不起的人，然后是惊叹这个动作，最后指故事里的奇景奇谈。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: raised eyes and a silent gasp at something huge.
core.cn: 核心意象：抬起头睁大眼睛，被庞然之物惊得屏住呼吸。

branches.en: The wonderful thing is the leading sense.
branches.cn: 奇妙之物是最核心的义项。

branches.en: The sense moves from things to people.
branches.cn: 义项从事物转移到人身上。

branches.en: The verb is the feeling turned into action.
branches.cn: 动词义就是把感受变成了动作。

branches.en: Both engineering feats and story wonders amaze us.
branches.cn: 工程的壮举与故事里的奇景都会让人惊叹。

branches.en: An amazing person is exactly what people marvel at.
branches.cn: 了不起的人正是人们会惊叹、钦佩的对象。

intro.en: Marvel comes through French from the Latin wonder family, leaving English with marvellous, marvelously, and the related word miracle.
intro.cn: marvel 经法语从拉丁语的「惊奇」词族传来，在英语中留下 marvellous、marvelously，以及与它相关的 miracle。

latinIntro.en: Latin mirari means to wonder, and mirabilia means wonderful things.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mirari 意为惊叹、感到疑惑，mirabilia 意为奇妙之事。

items.example: Mirari is the root of the wonder family.
items.exampleCN: mirari 是整个「惊奇」词族的根。

items.example: Mirabilia lies behind the French form.
items.exampleCN: mirabilia 是法语词形背后的来源。

items.example: Merveille comes from the Latin forms above.
items.exampleCN: merveille 来自上面所说的拉丁语词形。

items.example: Marvel settles in English in the medieval period.
items.exampleCN: marvel 在中世纪英语里定型。

items.example: The verb is usually followed by at.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词后面通常跟 at。

items.example: The suffix -ous forms marvellous.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 构成 marvellous。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms marvelously.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 marvelously。

items.example: Miracle shares the Latin wonder root.
items.exampleCN: miracle 共享拉丁语「惊奇」词根。

items.example: The plural simply adds -s.
items.exampleCN: 复数形式只是加一个 -s。

definition_zh: 屠杀；杀戮；惨案；大败
definition_en: the cruel killing of many people at once, or to kill many people in this way
core_image: 一群人被围在空地上，几乎没有还手的机会
scene: 古战场上，弱势一方被围困在城下，几乎无人逃脱。The invading soldiers massacred the townspeople who could not flee.
sceneCN: 这里 massacre 是「屠杀」（第 1 个义项：大批地杀害无还手之力的人）；句意：入侵的士兵屠杀了无法逃走的市民。

pos.zh: 屠杀；大批杀害；彻底击败

collocations.phrase: suffer a massacre on the field

derivatives.zh: 基础词加 -er 构成，指参与屠杀的人，较少用
动词加 -ing 构成的名词，指屠杀行为
过去分词作形容词，指被大批杀害的

senses.title: The killing of many people
senses.definition: the cruel and deliberate killing of a large number of people, especially those who cannot defend themselves
senses.definitionCN: 残酷而蓄意地杀害大批人，尤其是无力自卫者
senses.example: The village massacre shocked the whole country.
senses.exampleCN: 那场村庄屠杀震惊了全国。
senses.why: French massacre named a slaughter, a butchering of animals, and the image of a whole group struck down at once survives in the modern word.
senses.whyCN: 法语 massacre 本指宰杀、屠宰，整个群体同时被放倒的画面一直保留到现代英语里。

senses.title: The act as a named event
senses.definition: a particular event in which many people are killed, often remembered by place or date
senses.definitionCN: 许多人被杀害的具体事件，常以地点或日期被记住
senses.example: Historians still argue about the causes of the massacre.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家至今仍在争论那场惨案的起因。
senses.why: Once the act became famous, people stopped using it as an activity and began using it as a named event in history.
senses.whyCN: 这个行为一旦出名，人们就不再把它当作一种活动，而是当作历史中一个有名目的事件。

senses.title: To kill many people
senses.definition: to kill a large number of people or animals in a cruel and uncontrolled way
senses.definitionCN: 残忍而不加克制地杀害大批人或动物
senses.example: Troops massacred hundreds of prisoners in the night.
senses.exampleCN: 军队在夜里屠杀了数百名囚犯。
senses.why: English turned the noun into a verb so that the slaughter could be described from the killer side, as one action.
senses.whyCN: 英语把这个名词转为动词，好从行凶者一方把整场杀戮说成一个动作。

senses.title: A crushing defeat
senses.definition: a very heavy defeat in a game, election, or argument
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、选举或争论中遭受的极惨重的失败
senses.example: Our team suffered a massacre on Saturday.
senses.exampleCN: 我们队周六遭遇了一场惨败。
senses.why: If killing everyone is a total loss of life, an overwhelming defeat is a total loss of a contest, so sportswriters borrowed the word.
senses.whyCN: 屠尽所有人等于生命的彻底丧失，压倒性的失败则是竞赛的彻底丧失，体育记者便借用了这个词。

senses.title: To defeat completely
senses.definition: to defeat an opponent very heavily, especially in sport
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛等场合以压倒性优势击败对手
senses.example: The champions massacred the visitors by five goals to nil.
senses.exampleCN: 冠军队以五比零狠狠击败了客队。
senses.why: The verb sense of total destruction extends easily to a contest: one side is wiped out while the other is untouched.
senses.whyCN: 动词义里「彻底毁掉」的意思很容易延伸到竞赛：一方被消灭，另一方却毫发无损。

intro.en: Massacre comes from the Old French noun massacre, a slaughter, which goes back to an Old French verb meaning to butcher animals.
intro.cn: massacre 来自古法语名词 massacre（杀戮），再上溯到一个意为「屠宰牲畜」的古法语动词。

items.en: The root behind the Old French verb is usually traced to macellare, to butcher, though the exact mediæval form is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为古法语动词源于拉丁语 macellare（屠宰），但确切的中世纪形式尚不确定。

items.en: Massacre names the killing of animals in a shambles or slaughterhouse, not yet used for people.
items.cn: 古法语 massacre 指在肉铺或屠宰场宰杀牲畜，当时还不用于人。

items.en: The meaning stretches from butchering animals to the slaughter of human beings.
items.cn: 从宰杀牲畜扩展为残杀人类。

items.en: English borrows the noun from French and uses it first for the killing of people who cannot defend themselves.
items.cn: 英语从法语借入该名词，最初指杀害无力自卫的人。

items.en: The word is soon used as a verb, so that troops are said to massacre a town.
items.cn: 这个词很快被用作动词，于是可以说军队屠杀一座城镇。

items.en: Sportswriters extend the word to crushing defeats, and historians use it for named atrocities.
items.cn: 体育记者把这词扩展到惨败，历史学家则用它指有名目的暴行。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the Old French and Latin family and two words that only look close; the near-meaning group grades violence and defeat by how total they are.
note.cn: 形近组收录古法语与拉丁语同族词，以及两个只是长得像的词；近义组按彻底程度区分暴力与失败。

entries.definition: having been killed in large numbers
entries.definitionCN: 同根：限制式分词，意为「被大批杀害的」。

entries.definition: the Italian cognate, a slaughter
entries.definitionCN: 同源意大利语形式，意为屠杀。

entries.definition: Latin verb meaning to butcher
entries.definitionCN: 同根拉丁语动词，意为屠宰。

entries.definition: the killing of many people or animals cruelly
entries.definitionCN: 近义：残忍地杀死大批人或动物，也可指屠宰。

entries.definition: the violent killing of many people in war
entries.definitionCN: 偏正式，多指战场上大量流血死亡。

entries.definition: an extremely cruel and shocking act
entries.definitionCN: 骇人听闻的暴行；强调行为的残暴，而不只是人数。

normalIntro.en: Massacre began in the shambles as a word for butchering animals and kept its scale and its cruelty.
normalIntro.cn: massacre 从屠宰场里的宰杀开始，一路保留着「规模」与「残忍」两个特点。

normal.en: Mass begins with mass, a word for a body of masses of people.
normal.cn: 词头 mass 提示「大量、成群」，被屠杀的是一群人。

normal.en: Massacre shares its French ancestry with macellare, a butchering verb.
normal.cn: massacre 与表示屠宰的拉丁语 macellare 同出法语一脉。

normal.en: Commit a massacre is the standard verb partner for the noun.
normal.cn: commit a massacre 是名词最常用的动词搭配。

normal.en: The massacre of civilians makes the victim group explicit.
normal.cn: the massacre of civilians 直接点出受害群体。

normal.en: Compare slaughter: massacre stresses a helpless group, while slaughter also means killing animals for meat.
normal.cn: 对比 slaughter：massacre 强调无助的群体，slaughter 还可指宰杀牲畜作肉食。

abstract.en: Picture a town square where no one can escape.
abstract.cn: 想象一个广场，没有人能逃走。

abstract.en: Hear it as a single word for one terrible event on a calendar.
abstract.cn: 把它想成日历上某个可怕事件的名字。

abstract.en: See a scoreboard at five to nil and call the thrashing a massacre.
abstract.cn: 想象比分牌上五比零，把这场血洗叫作惨败。

examples.en: The massacre of the village was never formally investigated.
examples.cn: 那座村庄的屠杀从未被正式调查。

examples.en: The army was accused of massacring civilians during the raid.
examples.cn: 该军队被控在突袭中屠杀平民。

examples.en: The press described the final match as a massacre.
examples.cn: 媒体把决赛形容成一场惨败。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「 massacr 」读来像「马萨克」，可以联想成「马被萨克（一把刀）放倒」，但这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 massacre（屠杀）← 古法语动词「屠宰牲畜」，一般认为再上溯拉丁语 macellare（屠宰），核心义「成批地被宰杀」。

sensesIntro.en: Massacre starts as a word for slaughtering animals, becomes the killing of many helpless people, is named as a historical event, then moves from violence to sporting defeat.
sensesIntro.cn: massacre 从屠宰牲畜起家，转指大批无力自卫者被杀，再成为历史事件的名目，最后从暴力滑向竞赛中的惨败。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowd with nowhere to run.
core.cn: 核心意象：一群无处可逃的人。

branches.en: The killing of a helpless crowd is the direct heir of the butchery sense.
branches.cn: 杀害无助的人群是「屠宰」义最直接的继承人。

branches.en: A massacre as a named event turns the act into a piece of history.
branches.cn: 义项二是把行为固化为一段历史的事件。

branches.en: The verb describes the same act from the side of the killers.
branches.cn: 义项三是从行凶者一侧描述同一行为。

branches.en: Total destruction of people and total defeat in a contest share the image of a wipe-out.
branches.cn: 人被杀光与比赛被彻底击败共享「一方被抹掉」的画面。

branches.en: The heavy defeat as a noun and the strong verb are two sides of the scoreboard.
branches.cn: 名词的惨败与动词的痛击是比分牌的两面。

intro.en: Massacre is a borrowed French noun plus verb; its parts come from the butchery root and from the -re ending of Old French.
intro.cn: massacre 是借自法语的名词兼动词，构件包括表示屠宰的词根和古法语的 -re 词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb macellare means to butcher, and the meat market macellum stands behind the Old French family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词 macellare 意为屠宰，肉市 macellum 是古法语一族词形的源头背景。

items.example: Macellare supplies the butchery root.
items.exampleCN: macellare 提供「屠宰」词根。

items.example: Macellum is the market where carcasses are cut.
items.exampleCN: macellum 是切肉的市场。

items.example: Massacre enters English from this French noun.
items.exampleCN: massacre 从这个法语名词进入英语。

items.example: The Old French verb turns the noun into an action.
items.exampleCN: 这个古法语动词把名词变成动作。

items.example: The verb arrives soon after the noun.
items.exampleCN: 动词在名词之后不久出现。

items.example: The suffix gives the rare massacrer.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成较少用的 massacrer。

items.meaningCN: 表示被动与完成的词尾
items.example: The suffix forms massacred.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 massacred。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或过程的词尾
items.example: The suffix forms massacring.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 massacring。

definition_zh: 按摩；推拿；揉搓；美化数字
definition_en: the act of rubbing and pressing the body to relax muscles or ease pain, or to rub and press something repeatedly
core_image: 一双手沿着紧绷的肩背慢慢推压，肌肉一点点松开
scene: 他搬了一天的箱子，肩膀酸得抬不起来，妻子叫他去做个放松。He had a massage after work and felt his stiff shoulders relax.
sceneCN: 这里 massage 是「按摩」（第 1 个义项：用手推揉按捏身体以放松）；句意：他下班后做了按摩，觉得僵硬的肩膀松开了。

pos.zh: 按摩；揉按；美化（数字、说辞）

collocations.zh: 软磨硬泡地劝某人做某事

derivatives.zh: 男按摩师，借自法语
女按摩师，借自法语
动词加 -ing 构成的名词，指按摩这一动作

senses.title: The health treatment
senses.definition: the rubbing and pressing of muscles, usually by a trained person, to relax the body or ease pain
senses.definitionCN: 由受过训练的人揉捏按压肌肉，以放松身体或缓解疼痛
senses.example: She booked a massage for her aching back.
senses.exampleCN: 她为酸痛的背预约了按摩。
senses.why: The French verb masser means to knead, to press something soft with the hands, so the treatment inherits the action of working dough.
senses.whyCN: 法语动词 masser 意为揉面、捏压，这个疗法继承的正是揉面团一般的手上动作。

senses.title: Rubbing and pressing part of the body
senses.definition: the action of rubbing or kneading a part of the body with the hands
senses.definitionCN: 用手揉按或推压身体的某个部位
senses.example: A massage of the feet can help you sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 按摩双脚有助于睡眠。
senses.why: The noun can still name the bare physical action, not the whole treatment session.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词也仍可只指单纯的物理动作，而不指完整的疗程。

senses.title: To rub and press a body
senses.definition: to rub and press someone muscles, especially to help them relax
senses.definitionCN: 揉按某人的肌肉，尤指帮助其放松
senses.example: The nurse massaged his legs to improve circulation.
senses.exampleCN: 护士给他的双腿按摩以促进血液循环。
senses.why: English turned the French verb into a verb of its own, so the word no longer needs a noun partner.
senses.whyCN: 英语把法语动词借过来自己当动词用，于是不必再借助名词。

senses.title: To press something repeatedly with the hands
senses.definition: to press and move a thing with the hands again and again
senses.definitionCN: 用双手反复按压并移动某物
senses.example: She massaged the cream into her hands.
senses.exampleCN: 她把乳霜揉进双手。
senses.why: The original kneading image covers any soft substance, from dough to skin, so the verb reaches beyond the body.
senses.whyCN: 最初「揉面」的画面涵盖任何柔软之物，从面团到皮肤，于是动词超出身体范围。

senses.title: To make figures look better
senses.definition: to change facts or figures in a careful way so that they look better, often dishonestly
senses.definitionCN: 小心地改动数据或事实，使其显得更好，常含欺骗意味
senses.example: Critics accused the company of massaging the statistics.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者指责公司美化了统计数据。
senses.why: Kneading means pressing something until its shape pleases you, so massaging figures is shaping numbers until they look good.
senses.whyCN: 揉捏意味着按压某物直到形状合己意，所以美化数据就是把数字揉到自己满意。

senses.title: To flatter or persuade gently
senses.definition: to flatter someone or persuade them slowly and gently
senses.definitionCN: 奉承某人，或慢慢地软磨硬泡说服对方
senses.example: He spent the evening massaging the editor ego.
senses.exampleCN: 他整晚都在迎合那位编辑的自尊心。
senses.why: If the self can be treated like something soft that can be smoothed with the hands, flattery is a massage given to another person pride.
senses.whyCN: 如果把「自我」当作能被双手抚平的软物，奉承就是给别人的自尊做按摩。

intro.en: Massage comes from the French verb masser, to knead, whose origin is uncertain and is often linked by folk etymology to the Arabic word massa, to touch.
intro.cn: massage 来自法语动词 masser（揉捏），其来源不确定，常被民间词源联系到阿拉伯语 massa（触摸）。

items.en: French masser means to knead or work a soft mass with the hands, like dough.
items.cn: 法语 masser 意为用手揉捏、加工柔软的团块，像揉面团一样。

items.en: The link with the Arabic word for to touch is popular, but the accepted account treats it as a guess.
items.cn: 与阿拉伯语「触摸」一词的联系很流行，但一般只把它当作一种猜测。

items.en: The origin is uncertain; scholars do not agree whether the French verb came from mass, the lump of dough, or from elsewhere.
items.cn: 来源不确定：学者们尚未就这个法语动词是来自 mass（面团块）还是别处达成一致。

items.en: English borrows massage as a medical and Indian or French practice in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 十九世纪英语把 massage 作为医学疗法与来自印度或法国的做法借入。

items.en: The word widens from clinics to spas, sports and hotels.
items.cn: 这个词从诊所扩展到水疗、运动与酒店。

items.en: Figurative senses of smoothing a self, an ego, or figures spread in journalism and business.
items.cn: 抚平自我、自尊或数据的比喻义在新闻与商业语言中扩散。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the French massage family and one dangerous neighbour in spelling; the near-meaning group covers the hands-on cures and the smoothing metaphors.
note.cn: 形近组保留法语 mass 词族的按摩词，并提醒一个拼写相近的危险邻居；近义组涵盖手上的疗法与「抚平」类比喻。

entries.definition: a man whose job is to rub and press people muscles
entries.definitionCN: 同根派生：男按摩师。

entries.definition: a woman whose job is to rub and press people muscles
entries.definitionCN: 同根派生：女按摩师。

entries.definition: the French verb meaning to knead with the hands
entries.definitionCN: 同根法语动词，意为用手揉捏。

entries.definition: to move your hand over a surface with pressure
entries.definitionCN: 近义：用手加压移动，最普通的揉搓。

entries.definition: to press and shape a soft substance with your hands
entries.definitionCN: 与按摩同源的喻义：揉捏柔软之物。

entries.definition: treatment of injury by movement and physical methods
entries.definitionCN: 物理治疗，常与按摩一同用于康复。

normalIntro.en: Massage is the French kneading of hands on a soft mass, stretched from dough to muscle, to self, and to figures.
normalIntro.cn: massage 是法语里双手揉捏一团软物的动作，从面团延伸到肌肉、自我与数据。

normal.en: Massage comes from mass, a lump of dough that the hands press and turn.
normal.cn: massage 与 mass（一团面团）相关，双手揉压翻动它。

normal.en: Have a massage and give someone a massage are the two common verb partners.
normal.cn: have a massage 与 give someone a massage 是名词最常用的两种搭配。

normal.en: Masseur and masseuse are the person nouns borrowed with the treatment.
normal.cn: masseur 与 masseuse 是与疗法一起借来的施动名词。

normal.en: The -age ending comes straight from French, as in other French loans.
normal.cn: 结尾的 -age 直接来自法语，与其他法语借词一致。

normal.en: Compare rub: rub is any hand movement, while massage is repeated pressing with a purpose.
normal.cn: 对比 rub：rub 只是任何手部移动，massage 是有目的、反复的按压。

abstract.en: Feel two hands walk slowly down a stiff shoulder blade.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手沿着僵硬的肩胛骨慢慢向下推。

abstract.en: See a masseur working dough the way a baker does.
abstract.cn: 把按摩想象成按摩师像面包师一样揉面团。

abstract.en: Watch a spreadsheet being squeezed until the totals improve.
abstract.cn: 想象一张表格被揉压到总数变得好看。

examples.en: The hotel offers a massage after every long hike.
examples.cn: 这家酒店在每次长途徒步后都提供按摩。

examples.en: He massaged his tired feet before going to bed.
examples.cn: 睡前他按摩了酸痛的双脚。

examples.en: The team was accused of massaging the funding figures.
examples.cn: 该团队被指责美化了资助数据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马杀鸡」——这是流行多年的谐音叫法，读音相近，但只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 法语 masser（揉捏、揉面团）+-age 名词词尾 → massage；来源不确定，与 mass（面团块）关系密切，核心义「用手反复揉压」。

sensesIntro.en: Massage holds one physical action, kneading with the hands, which becomes a health treatment, a verb for touching a body or a cream, and then a metaphor for smoothing figures and feelings.
sensesIntro.cn: massage 的核心只有一个手上动作，即揉捏，它伸展为一种疗法，变成给身体或乳霜揉按的动词，再比喻为把数字与情绪「揉平」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands kneading a soft mass.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手揉捏一团柔软的东西。

branches.en: The treatment is the kneading action applied to muscles.
branches.cn: 疗法就是把揉捏的动作施加到肌肉上。

branches.en: The act sense keeps only the bare rubbing, without the whole session.
branches.cn: 义项二只保留单纯的揉按动作，不含完整疗程。

branches.en: The verb lets English say directly that someone massages a body.
branches.cn: 动词义让英语可以直接说某人给人按摩。

branches.en: Muscles and cream are both soft substances pressed by the hands.
branches.cn: 肌肉与乳霜都是被双手按压的柔软之物。

branches.en: Figures and egos are both kneaded until they look or feel better.
branches.cn: 数据与自尊都像被揉捏过，变得更好看、更好受。

intro.en: Massage is built on the French noun mass plus the -age ending, with masseur and masseuse borrowed on the same pattern.
intro.cn: massage 由法语名词 mass 加 -age 词尾构成，masseur 与 masseuse 也按同一模式借入。

latinIntro.en: Latin has no claimed origin for massage; the French mass is usually linked to a Romance word for a mass of dough rather than to a classical Latin verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语并不能为 massage 提供确证的来源；法语 mass 一般被联系到罗曼语里表示「面团块」的词，而非某个古典拉丁动词。

items.meaning: a mass, a lump of dough
items.example: Mass is the lump the hands work on.
items.exampleCN: mass 是被双手揉压的那团东西。

items.example: Masser is the direct source of the verb.
items.exampleCN: masser 是动词的直接来源。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或结果的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -age turns masser into massage.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -age 把 masser 变成 massage。

items.meaning: to rub and press a body
items.example: The verb also means to smooth figures.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词也指修饰数据。

items.example: The suffix -eur forms masseur.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -eur 构成 masseur。

items.example: The suffix -euse forms masseuse.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -euse 构成 masseuse。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或过程的词尾
items.example: The suffix forms massaging.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 massaging。

items.example: Masser gives the repeated pressing image.
items.exampleCN: masser 提供「反复按压」的画面。

definition_zh: 主谋；幕后策划者；才智出众者；策划（尤指复杂或犯罪计划）
definition_en: a person who plans and directs a complicated activity, usually a crime, or to plan and direct such an activity
core_image: 一个人坐在桌边把一张大网的所有线头都收在手里
scene: 侦探查了几个月，终于发现抢案背后有一个从不出面、只在图纸上安排每一步的人。The detective finally identified the man who had masterminded the robbery.
sceneCN: 这里 mastermind 是「策划」（第 1 个义项：像主谋一样精密地安排并指挥）；句意：侦探终于查出了策划这场抢劫的那个人。

pos.zh: 策划；精心策划（尤指罪案）

derivatives.zh: 动词加 -ing 构成的名词，指策划过程
过去分词作形容词，指由智囊精心安排的
由 master 加 -ly 构成的形容词，意为精湛的

senses.title: The planner of a complicated scheme
senses.definition: a person who plans and organizes a complicated activity, especially a crime or trick
senses.definitionCN: 策划并组织复杂活动的人，尤指犯罪或计谋
senses.example: Police are still looking for the mastermind of the fraud.
senses.exampleCN: 警方仍在寻找那起诈骗案的主谋。
senses.why: Master plus mind says a mind that masters a plan, so the word first names a brain that controls a whole design.
senses.whyCN: master（精通）与 mind（头脑）相连，意思是能驾驭整个计划的头脑，所以这个词首先指掌控全局的大脑。

senses.title: The brilliant person
senses.definition: a very intelligent person, especially one who shows skill in a field
senses.definitionCN: 非常聪明的人，尤指在某一领域显露才华者
senses.example: She is the marketing mastermind of the group.
senses.exampleCN: 她是这个集团里营销方面的天才。
senses.why: If mastering a scheme shows a strong mind, then anyone with such a mind can simply be called a mastermind.
senses.whyCN: 既然驾驭一套计划能显出强健的头脑，那么拥有这种头脑的人也可以直接叫作 mastermind。

senses.title: To plan a complicated act
senses.definition: to plan and organize a complicated activity or crime
senses.definitionCN: 策划并组织复杂的活动或罪案
senses.example: He masterminded the whole escape from his cell.
senses.exampleCN: 他精心策划了整场越狱。
senses.why: The noun of the planning brain became a verb, so the action of acting as that brain is now a single verb.
senses.whyCN: 代表「策划之脑」的名词变成了动词，于是充当这颗大脑的行为如今可以用一个动词说出。

senses.title: To design a campaign or scheme
senses.definition: to plan and direct a campaign, project, or policy
senses.definitionCN: 策划并指挥一场运动、项目或政策
senses.example: The consultant masterminded the new recycling programme.
senses.exampleCN: 这位顾问统筹策划了新的回收计划。
senses.why: The verb keeps the crime flavour but steps outside it, because a campaign also needs a single mind holding the threads.
senses.whyCN: 动词仍带着「罪案」的意味，却跨出了罪案，因为一场运动也需要一颗头脑把所有线头握在手里。

intro.en: Mastermind is an English compound of master, from Latin magister, and mind, from the Germanic word for memory and thought.
intro.cn: mastermind 是英语复合词：master 来自拉丁语 magister，mind 来自日耳曼语中表示「记忆与思想」的词。

items.en: Magister means a teacher or chief, from magis, more, the one who is greater.
items.cn: magister 意为老师或首领，来自 magis（更多），即更优胜的人。

items.en: Gemynd means memory and thought; Modern English mind comes from this Germanic root.
items.cn: 古英语 gemynd 意为记忆与思想，现代 mind 即由此来。

items.en: Maistre carries magister into French and then into Middle English as master or mister.
items.cn: maistre 把 magister 传入法语，再以 master 或 mister 的形式进入中古英语。

items.en: Master already covers both skill and authority, so it joins well with mind.
items.cn: master 当时已兼指技艺与权威，因此与 mind 结合十分自然。

items.en: The compound mastermind appears in the late nineteenth century, first as a noun for a superior mind.
items.cn: 复合词 mastermind 出现于十九世纪后期，最初作为名词指卓越的头脑。

items.en: Detective fiction and crime reports fix the sense of the clever planner behind a crime.
items.cn: 侦探小说与犯罪报道固定了「罪案背后精明的策划者」这一含义。

note.en: The look-alike group splits the compound into master and mind and adds words formed on each part; the near-meaning group names planners, schemers and clever people.
note.cn: 形近组把复合词拆成 master 与 mind，并补充各部件构成的词；近义组则收录策划者、阴谋家与聪明人。

entries.definition: a person with great skill or authority
entries.definitionCN: 复合词前半：技艺高超或有权的人。

entries.definition: the ability to think, reason, and remember
entries.definitionCN: 复合词后半：思考、推理与记忆的能力。

entries.definition: a fixed way of thinking
entries.definitionCN: 同根复合词：mindset 意为思维方式。

entries.definition: a very clever act or plan
entries.definitionCN: 近义：极为高明的一着；指行为本身。

entries.definition: a person who secretly makes plans
entries.definitionCN: 爱暗中谋划的人，多含贬义。

entries.definition: a person who organizes a complex activity
entries.definitionCN: 近义：统筹复杂的活动者。

normalIntro.en: Mastermind glues a master of a craft to a mind, so the brain that masters the plan gets the name.
normalIntro.cn: mastermind 把「某行的大师」与「头脑」粘在一起，于是驾驭计划的那颗大脑就有了名字。

normal.en: Master comes from Latin magister, a teacher or chief.
normal.cn: master 来自拉丁语 magister，意为老师或首领。

normal.en: Mind shares a Germanic root with memory, so it is the thinking part.
normal.cn: mind 与「记忆」同出日耳曼词根，指的是思考的部分。

normal.en: The mastermind behind the plot is the usual noun frame.
normal.cn: the mastermind behind the plot 是名词最常用的框架。

normal.en: Mastermind a robbery puts the word in the planning seat, like mastermind other schemes.
normal.cn: mastermind a robbery 把词放进「策划」的位置，与 mastermind other schemes 同型。

normal.en: Compare genius: genius is born, a mastermind is usually a planner.
normal.cn: 对比 genius：genius 多指天生才华，mastermind 通常指精于布局的人。

abstract.en: Picture a spider at the centre of a finished web.
abstract.cn: 想象一只蜘蛛坐在织好的网的正中央。

abstract.en: See a chess player moving five pieces in one thought.
abstract.cn: 想象一位棋手一个念头就挪动五枚棋子。

abstract.en: Hear maps and blueprints pinned to a wall in one quiet room.
abstract.cn: 想象一间安静的屋子里，墙上钉满地图与蓝图。

examples.en: The police believe the accountant was the mastermind of the fraud.
examples.cn: 警方认为那名会计是这起诈骗案的主谋。

examples.en: She masterminded a campaign that changed the whole industry.
examples.cn: 她策划了一场改变整个行业的运动。

examples.en: Everyone called him the mastermind of the operation.
examples.cn: 大家都称他是这次行动的主脑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「 master + 头脑」——大师的头脑，自然是策划全局的人；这只是拆词联想，与词源构词有关但非严格词源。

root: 英语复合词 master（拉丁语 magister，大师、首领）+ mind（古英语 gemynd，记忆、思想），核心义「驾驭全局的头脑」。

sensesIntro.en: Mastermind starts with the brain that masters a plan, widens to any brilliant person, then turns into the verb of designing a crime or a campaign.
sensesIntro.cn: mastermind 先指驾驭计划的那颗头脑，扩而泛指任何才智出众者，再转为策划罪案或运动的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one quiet person holding every thread of a plan.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个安静的人握着整张计划的所有线头。

branches.en: The planner of a scheme is the core compound sense.
branches.cn: 义项一是复合词的核心义：复杂计划的策划者。

branches.en: A mind that masters so much can simply be called brilliant.
branches.cn: 义项二由「能驾驭全局的头脑」放宽为「天才」。

branches.en: The verb names the work of that mind.
branches.cn: 义项三把那颗头脑所做的功变成一个动词。

branches.en: A bright organizer and a campaign planner share the same skill.
branches.cn: 天才的组织者与运动策划者共享同一种本领。

branches.en: The noun names the person and the verb names the act.
branches.cn: 名词指人，动词指其所做的策划。

intro.en: Mastermind is a native English compound; master is a Latin loan through French, and mind is inherited from Old English.
intro.cn: mastermind 是英语本土复合词：master 经法语借自拉丁语，mind 则继承自古英语。

latinIntro.en: Latin magister, a teacher or chief, comes from magis, more, and gives English master, mastery and magistrate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 magister（老师、首领）来自 magis（更多），并衍生出英语的 master、mastery 与 magistrate。

items.example: Magis gives the idea of being greater.
items.exampleCN: magis 提供「更优胜」的意思。

items.example: Magister is the source of master.
items.exampleCN: magister 是 master 的来源。

items.example: Maistre carries magister into French.
items.exampleCN: maistre 把 magister 带入法语。

items.meaning: a person with skill or authority
items.example: Master is the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: master 是复合词的前半。

items.example: The suffix forms mastery from master.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把 master 构成 mastery。

items.example: Mind is the second half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: mind 是复合词的后半。

items.example: Gemynd is the older form of mind.
items.exampleCN: gemynd 是 mind 的较早形式。

items.example: Mind also builds other compounds such as mindset.
items.exampleCN: mind 还能构成 mindset 这类复合词。

items.example: The compound appears in the late nineteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词出现于十九世纪后期。

definition_zh: 精通；熟练；掌握；控制；支配；征服；导师身份
definition_en: complete skill or control in a subject, craft, or difficult situation
core_image: 一个学徒最终稳稳握住工具，动作不再迟疑
scene: 练了十年之后，那位陶艺师拉坯时手几乎不用思考。After ten years of practice, the potter throws clay with a calm mastery of the wheel.
sceneCN: 这里 mastery 是「熟练掌握、精通」（第 1 个义项：通过长期练习获得的高超技艺）；句意：十年练习之后，陶艺师以沉稳的熟练控制着拉坯轮。

pos.zh: 精通；熟练；掌握；控制；支配；征服

derivatives.zh: 主人；大师；硕士，master 加名词后缀 -y 构成 mastery
技艺高超的；专横的，由 master 加形容词后缀 -ful 构成
功力精湛的，由 master 加形容词后缀 -ly 构成
以大师般的手法，加 -ly 后可作副词用

senses.title: Great skill in a subject
senses.definition: a very high level of skill in a language, art, craft, or subject
senses.definitionCN: 在语言、艺术、手艺或学科上达到的极高熟练程度
senses.example: Her mastery of Spanish surprised the examiners.
senses.exampleCN: 她对西班牙语的精通让考官们感到惊讶。
senses.why: Mastery comes from master, a learned person in Latin; the noun then names the quality of having become such a person.
senses.whyCN: mastery 来自 master，拉丁语里指学业有成、取得硕士学位的人；名词因此表示「已经成为这样的人」所带来的那种水平。

senses.title: Control of a skill or tool
senses.definition: the ability to use a skill, tool, or technique with full control
senses.definitionCN: 能完全自如地运用某项技艺、工具或方法的能力
senses.example: The surgeon shows impressive mastery of the new instrument.
senses.exampleCN: 这位外科医生对新器械的掌控令人印象深刻。
senses.why: The medieval master controlled a workshop, so mastery naturally moved from rank to the control that rank demanded.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪的 master 掌管着一整间工坊，于是 mastery 从「师父的身份」顺着滑到了这种身份所要求的「掌控力」。

senses.title: Power to dominate something
senses.definition: power or authority to control a situation, resource, or other people
senses.definitionCN: 控制局面、资源或他人所拥有的力量与权威
senses.example: The firm seeks mastery of the regional market.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司谋求控制区域市场。
senses.why: A master owns and commands, so the noun extends from controlling a tool to controlling a market, a rival, or a crowd.
senses.whyCN: master 既有「拥有」又是「指挥者」，所以这个词从掌控工具延伸到掌控市场、对手或人群。

senses.title: Physical command of movement
senses.definition: the ability to move or use the body with confident precision
senses.definitionCN: 能以自信而精准的方式活动或使用身体的能力
senses.example: The climber held the ledge with quiet mastery.
senses.exampleCN: 攀登者以一种沉静的自如扣住岩沿。
senses.why: Skill needs a body, and mastery names that same exact control when hands and balance obey without hesitation.
senses.whyCN: 技艺要靠身体来完成，mastery 也用来指双手与重心毫不犹豫地听命时的精确控制。

senses.title: Emotional self-command
senses.definition: the ability to keep your emotions and impulses under control
senses.definitionCN: 把自己的情绪和冲动控制在手中的能力
senses.example: She answered the insult with complete mastery of her temper.
senses.exampleCN: 面对侮辱，她完全克制住了自己的脾气。
senses.why: The object being controlled can also be oneself, and mastery of the emotions is a favourite phrase in moral writing.
senses.whyCN: 被掌控的对象也可以是自己，对情绪的 mastery 在道德与修养类文字里尤为常见。

senses.title: Victory over a difficulty
senses.definition: the act of overcoming a hard problem, fear, or enemy
senses.definitionCN: 战胜难题、恐惧或敌人的行为
senses.example: His mastery of the final climb took years.
senses.exampleCN: 他征服最后一段攀登用了好几年。
senses.why: If you command a thing you have also beaten it, so mastery comes to name the winning of a struggle.
senses.whyCN: 能支配某物，也就等于战胜了它，于是 mastery 用来命名一场较量的胜利。

senses.title: The state of a master
senses.definition: the title, position, or authority of a master or teacher
senses.definitionCN: 师父、教师这一头衔、职位或权威
senses.example: Under his mastery the guild trained three new founders.
senses.exampleCN: 在他的师道之下，行会培养出了三位新铸工。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer: -y added to master makes an abstract noun for the rank itself, before any idea of skill.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层：master 加上名词后缀 -y 先造出表示「头衔本身」的抽象名词，那时还没有「技艺」的意思。

intro.en: Mastery is English master plus the noun suffix -y in the sense of state or quality; master itself traces to Latin magister, through Old English mægester and Old French maistre.
intro.cn: mastery 由英语 master 加表示状态或性质的名词后缀 -y 构成；master 本身可追溯到拉丁语 magister，经由古英语 mægester 与古法语 maistre 进入英语。

items.en: Magister means a chief, a teacher, or the master of a household; it comes from magis, more, with the comparative suffix -ter.
items.cn: magister 意为首领、教师或一家之主，源于对比形式 magis（更多）加后缀 -ter。

items.en: The borrowed form mægester names a teacher or a man of learning, and is used for the university degree of master.
items.cn: 借入的古英语形式 mægester 指教师或有学问的人，也用于大学的 master 学位。

items.en: Maistre keeps the everyday sense of a man in charge of servants, a trade, or a household.
items.cn: 古法语 maistre 保留日常意义，指管理仆从、某门手艺或一个家庭的人。

items.en: The English noun master gains the abstract derivative mastery, first for the rank or office of a master.
items.cn: 英语名词 master 派生抽象名词 mastery，最初指「师父」的头衔或职位。

items.en: From the authority of the master, mastery widens to mean complete skill, then dominance over people, markets, and feelings.
items.cn: 从师父的权威出发，mastery 扩展为「完全娴熟」，再扩展为对人、市场与情绪的支配。

items.en: Today mastery is mainly praise of high skill, and appears in education as a level or goal of learning.
items.cn: 今天 mastery 主要用于称赞高超技艺，在教育领域则作为学习的层级或目标。

note.en: Mastery sits between skill words such as expertise and proficiency, and control words such as command and dominance.
note.cn: mastery 一边靠近 expertise、proficiency 这类「技艺」词，一边靠近 command、dominance 这类「控制」词。

entries.definition: a person in charge, or a highly skilled craftsman
entries.definitionCN: master 在英语中加名词后缀 -y 构成 mastery 这一抽象名词

entries.definition: showing great skill, or (of a person) showing a wish to control
entries.definitionCN: 由 master 加 -ful 构成，褒义指技艺高超，贬义指专横

entries.definition: carried out with great skill
entries.definitionCN: 由 master 加 -ly 构成，形容作品或手法功力精深

entries.definition: a lesson given by an expert to advanced students
entries.definitionCN: master 与 class 组合成的复合词，指由名家指导高阶学员的课程

entries.definition: great knowledge or skill in a particular field
entries.definitionCN: 某一领域的高深知识与技巧，偏重知识面而非控制力

entries.definition: a good level of ability in something learned
entries.definitionCN: 对所学内容达到的良好水平，常与语言等级挂钩

entries.definition: the ability to use something well, especially a language
entries.definitionCN: 对语言等的良好运用能力，与 mastery 的控制义最接近

entries.definition: the state of being more powerful or important than others
entries.definitionCN: 支配地位，只有 mastery 的控制义，不含技艺义

normalIntro.en: Mastery is what a master has: first the title, later the skill and control that go with it.
normalIntro.cn: mastery 就是 master 所拥有的东西：先是头衔，后来是与之相配的技艺与掌控力。

normal.en: Remove the final letter -r of master and add -y to get mastery.
normal.cn: 把 master 末尾的 r 去掉再加 -y，就得到 mastery。

normal.en: The suffix -y turns a noun into an abstract noun of state, as in modest to modesty.
normal.cn: 后缀 -y 常把名词变成表示状态的名词，如 modest 变 modesty 一样。

normal.en: Mastery of a language is the standard phrase for near native ability.
normal.cn: mastery of a language 是用来表示接近母语水平的固定说法。

normal.en: Gain mastery over a habit means to bring it fully under control.
normal.cn: gain mastery over 后面既可接技能，也可接习惯或情绪，表示把它们完全控住。

normal.en: Compare mastery with expertise: expertise is knowing a lot, mastery is knowing and doing it perfectly.
normal.cn: 对比 expertise：expertise 偏重知识丰富，mastery 强调既能懂又能做到完美。

abstract.en: Picture an apprentice whose knife finally cuts straight without a single wobble.
abstract.cn: 想象一位学徒，手里的刀终于稳稳走直线，一次也不晃。（对应第 1 个义项：精通是长期练习后的熟练）

abstract.en: See a musician letting fingers find the strings before the mind gives an order.
abstract.cn: 想象一位乐手，手指在脑子里下命令之前就已经找到琴弦。（对应第 2 个义项：熟练就是对工具与动作的完全掌控）

abstract.en: Imagine a chess player quietly clearing the board of the opponent pieces.
abstract.cn: 想象一位棋手平静地把对手的棋子一一清走。（对应第 3 个义项：掌控局面就是能够支配对手）

examples.en: Students need several years to reach real mastery of academic writing.
examples.cn: 学生需要好几年才能真正掌握学术写作。

examples.en: The pilot showed remarkable mastery of the damaged aircraft.
examples.cn: 飞行员对受损飞机表现出非凡的掌控力。

examples.en: Mastery of a second language opens doors to other cultures.
examples.cn: 精通第二语言为通往其他文化打开大门。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「骂死他里」——把技术练到旁人挑不出毛病的程度，就是一种精通。这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 magister（首领、教师，源于 magis「更多」与对比后缀 -ter）→ 古英语 mægester → 古法语 maistre → 英语 master → master + 名词后缀 -y → mastery，核心义「师父所具备的东西」。

sensesIntro.en: Mastery starts from the rank of a master, then names the skill that rank demands, then the control such skill gives over tools, people, and oneself.
sensesIntro.cn: mastery 从「师父的头衔」出发，先指这种身份所要求的技艺，再指技艺带来的对工具、他人与自己的支配力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that holds a tool so surely that the motion needs no thought.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手稳稳握住工具，动作不再需要思考。

branches.en: Skill sense: the quality of a person who has mastered a field.
branches.cn: 技艺义：已经掌握某个领域的人所具备的品质。

branches.en: Control sense: full command of tools and of ones own movements.
branches.cn: 掌控义：对工具以及对自身动作的完全掌控。

branches.en: Power sense: domination over people, markets, or struggles.
branches.cn: 支配义：对他人、市场或较量的支配。

branches.en: Self sense: the same control turned inward on ones temper.
branches.cn: 内省义：把同样的掌控向内用于自己的脾气。

branches.en: Rank sense: the oldest use, naming the position of a master.
branches.cn: 身份义：最古老的用法，指师父的职位。

intro.en: Mastery is a suffix layer built on master, and the family grows with -ful and -ly, plus compounds such as master class.
intro.cn: mastery 是在 master 之上加后缀形成的一层，词族再用 -ful、-ly 扩展，并有 master class 这样的复合词。

latinIntro.en: The whole family rests on Latin magister, itself built from magis, more, and the comparative ending -ter.
latinIntro.cn: 整个词族建立在拉丁语 magister 之上，而 magister 又由 magis（更多）与对比后缀 -ter 构成。

items.meaning: a person in charge or an expert
items.example: The master teaches, and mastery names what the master has.
items.exampleCN: master 教人，mastery 则指 master 所具备的东西。

items.meaningCN: 状态或性质的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -y turns master into mastery.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 把 master 变成 mastery。

items.example: Mastery keeps both the skill sense and the power sense.
items.exampleCN: mastery 同时保留技艺义与支配义。

items.example: The suffix -ful forms masterful from master.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ful 由 master 构成 masterful。

items.example: Masterful is the adjective for skilled work and for a domineering manner.
items.exampleCN: masterful 既形容技艺高超的作品，也形容专横的态度。

items.meaningCN: 以……方式的形容词或副词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ly forms masterly from master.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 由 master 构成 masterly。

items.meaningCN: 功力精湛地；大师般的手法
items.example: Masterly usually praises a performance, not a person.
items.exampleCN: masterly 通常用来赞美表演或手法，而不是人。

items.meaning: a lesson by an expert for advanced learners
items.meaningCN: 名家给高阶学员上的课
items.example: A master class is where mastery is passed on.
items.exampleCN: master class 正是 mastery 得以传下去的地方。

items.example: Self-mastery applies the power sense to the self.
items.exampleCN: self-mastery 把「支配」这一层意义转向自己。

definition_zh: 无双的；无可匹敌的；无与伦比的
definition_en: so good or rare that nothing can be matched with it as an equal
core_image: 一张空着的对手席，没有谁能坐到对面来比一场
scene: 老将退役时，看台上所有人都承认再也找不到能与他相比的对手。When the veteran retired, the whole crowd knew his record was matchless.
sceneCN: 这里 matchless 是「无可匹敌的」（第 1 个义项：在某方面没有可匹配的对手）；句意：老将退役时，全场都知道他的纪录无人可匹敌。

pos.zh: 无双的；无可匹敌的；无与伦比的

derivatives.zh: 无与伦比地，matchless 加副词后缀 -ly 构成
无可匹敌，matchless 加名词后缀 -ness 构成
对手；相配之物，matchless 正是由 match 加否定后缀 -less 构成

senses.title: Having no equal in a contest
senses.definition: having no rival or competitor who can be set against you
senses.definitionCN: 没有任何对手或竞争者能与你相提并论
senses.example: As a fencer she remained matchless for a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 作为击剑手，她十余年间无人可敌。
senses.why: Match once meant a person fit to be an opponent, so matchless says that no such opponent exists.
senses.whyCN: match 早期就指「够格的对手」，matchless 直白地说出「这样的人都找不到」。

senses.title: So fine nothing compares
senses.definition: of such outstanding quality that nothing else can be compared with it
senses.definitionCN: 品质高得让别的一切都无法与之相比
senses.example: The cathedral has a matchless stained glass window.
senses.exampleCN: 这座大教堂有一扇无与伦比的彩绘玻璃窗。
senses.why: The same comparison logic works for things as for people: whatever has no match stands alone.
senses.whyCN: 这套比较逻辑对物也成立：找不到可配对的东西，它就独自耀眼。

senses.title: Rare and unrivalled beauty
senses.definition: used in literary praise for beauty or grace that seems unique
senses.definitionCN: 文学性的赞美，指美或优雅显得举世独一份
senses.example: They spoke of her matchless voice long after the concert.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐会结束很久之后，人们仍在谈论她举世无双的声音。
senses.why: Poets love the word because -less names an absence, and an absence of rivals sounds like praise.
senses.whyCN: 诗人偏爱这个词，因为 -less 表示「缺少」，而缺少对手听起来恰是最高的赞美。

intro.en: Matchless is English match plus the suffix -less; match itself comes from Old English gemæcca, a partner or equal, and the sense of a sporting contest developed later.
intro.cn: matchless 是英语 match 加后缀 -less 构成的；match 本身来自古英语 gemæcca（伴侣、对等者），「比赛」的意思则是后来才出现的。

items.en: A reconstructed form such as gamakjo is thought to give rise to the Old English word, though the prehistory of the root is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为古英语这个词源自一种重构形式（如 gamakjo），但这个词根的更早历史来源不确定。

items.en: Gemæcca means a mate, a partner, or a person of equal standing.
items.cn: 古英语 gemæcca 意为配偶、伙伴或地位相当的人。

items.en: The word shortens to macche and widens to anything paired or equal, including a contest between two sides.
items.cn: 中古英语里词形缩短为 macche，意义扩展到任何配对或相等之物，也包括双方对垒的赛事。

items.en: The suffix -less is attached to form matchless, first applied to people without a rival, then to things beyond compare.
items.cn: 加上否定后缀 -less 构成 matchless，起先形容无人可匹敌的人，后来也形容无可比拟的事物。

items.en: Matchless survives mainly as literary praise for beauty, skill, and courage, while literal contests prefer unrivaled.
items.cn: 现代英语中 matchless 主要作为文学性赞美，用于美、技艺与勇气；描写真实赛事时更多用 unrivaled 一类的词。

note.en: Matchless is one of a family of negative adjectives built with -less, and it sits with words meaning unequalled.
note.cn: matchless 是由 -less 构成的一系列否定形容词之一，意义靠近表示「无人能及」的一群词。

entries.definition: a contest, or a person equal to another
entries.definitionCN: match 本身指比赛，也指与某人相当的人；matchless 正是在它之上加否定后缀

entries.definition: not giving enough attention to what you do
entries.definitionCN: 同为 -less 结构，但 -less 在此表示「缺少谨慎」，并非「缺少对手」

entries.definition: unable to speak because of strong feeling
entries.definitionCN: 同为 -less 结构，表示「说不出话」的状态

entries.definition: a small folder of paper matches for lighting fires
entries.definitionCN: 这里 match 指火柴，只是拼写相近的词，词源与「对手」的 match 不同

entries.definition: better than any competitor
entries.definitionCN: 比任何竞争者都更强，英式拼写；美式写作 unrivaled

entries.definition: better than all others of its kind
entries.definitionCN: 没有同等者，语气极为文雅，多用于人物与作品

entries.definition: too good to be compared with anything else
entries.definitionCN: 好到无法比较，更强调无法并列这一点

entries.definition: being the only one of its kind
entries.definitionCN: 独一无二，只强调唯一，不一定含赞美

normalIntro.en: Matchless is match plus -less: take the suffix away and you have the word for a rival; keep it and the rival is gone.
normalIntro.cn: matchless 就是 match 加 -less：去掉后缀是「对手」，留下后缀对手就消失了。

normal.en: The suffix -less means without, as in hopeless and speechless.
normal.cn: 后缀 -less 表示「没有」，如 hopeless 与 speechless。

normal.en: Matchless therefore means without a match, that is, without an equal.
normal.cn: 所以 matchless 意为「没有 match」，也就是没有对等者。

normal.en: Matchless is normally written before a noun, as in matchless beauty.
normal.cn: matchless 一般放在名词前，如 matchless beauty。

normal.en: It is a strong but somewhat literary word, and modern sport writing usually says unbeaten or invincible.
normal.cn: 它语气强却略偏文雅，现代体育写作更常用 unbeaten 或 invincible。

normal.en: Compare peerless: peerless names the absence of a peer, matchless the absence of a match.
normal.cn: 对比 peerless：peerless 说缺的是「同辈」，matchless 说缺的是「对手」，二者都是否定式赞美。

abstract.en: Picture an empty chair across the board, waiting for an opponent who never comes.
abstract.cn: 想象棋盘对面空着一把椅子，等的对手始终没有出现。（对应第 1 个义项：找不到可匹敌的竞争者）

abstract.en: See a single perfect cup on a shelf with no second cup anywhere.
abstract.cn: 想象架子上只有一只完美的杯子，世间再找不出第二只与之配对。（对应第 2 个义项：品质高到无法比较）

abstract.en: Hear a voice so singular that listeners forget to clap.
abstract.cn: 想象一个声音独特到听众忘了鼓掌。（对应第 3 个义项：用于美貌、嗓音等文学性赞美）

examples.en: The old craftsman was matchless in the repair of violins.
examples.cn: 这位老匠人在修小提琴方面无人能及。

examples.en: Critics praised her matchless control of tone.
examples.cn: 评论家称赞她对音色无与伦比的掌控。

examples.en: Visitors describe the garden as matchless in early summer.
examples.cn: 游客们说这座花园在初夏时节举世无双。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「没吃力事」——凡事都显得没怎么费力就做到最好，旁人追不上，就是无可匹敌。这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 gemæcca（伴侣、对等者）→ 中古英语 macche（配对之物、比赛）→ 英语 match（对手；相配之物）→ match + 否定后缀 -less → matchless，核心义「没有可配对之物」。

sensesIntro.en: Matchless always names an absence of equal; it leans on people without rivals first, then on things beyond compare, and finally on literary praise of beauty.
sensesIntro.cn: matchless 始终表示「缺少对等者」：先用于没有对手的人，再用于无可比拟的事物，最后进入对美与才华的文学赞美。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty seat opposite, with no one able to sit down and take up the challenge.
core.cn: 核心意象：对面空着一个位子，无人敢坐下来应战。

branches.en: The contest sense: no opponent can be found.
branches.cn: 竞技义：找不到可以对抗的对手。

branches.en: The quality sense: nothing can be set beside it.
branches.cn: 品质义：没有任何东西能与它并列比较。

branches.en: The literary sense: praise of a unique beauty or voice.
branches.cn: 文学义：赞美独一无二的美貌或嗓音。

branches.en: Both senses rest on comparison, then deny that a comparison exists.
branches.cn: 前两个义项都建立在比较之上，再否定比较的存在。

branches.en: Descriptive excellence and poetic praise often share one word.
branches.cn: 客观的卓越与诗意的赞美常常共用同一个词。

intro.en: Matchless is a suffix construction on match, and the same -less or -ful family supplies matchless contrasts such as watchful.
intro.cn: matchless 是在 match 之上加后缀构词，同一组 -less 与 -ful 词族还能构出 watchful 这类对照词。

latinIntro.en: The match root is Germanic, not Latin; Latin comparisons such as aequalitas are useful only as conceptual parallels.
latinIntro.cn: match 的词根属日耳曼语而非拉丁语，此处列出的拉丁词只作概念对照，并非同源。

items.meaning: an equal, a contest, to pair
items.example: Match is the base on which matchless is built.
items.exampleCN: match 是 matchless 所依赖的词根。

items.example: The suffix -less turns match into matchless.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -less 把 match 变成 matchless。

items.example: Matchless is almost always used before a noun in praise.
items.exampleCN: matchless 几乎总放在名词前用于赞美。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms matchlessly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 matchlessly。

items.meaning: in a way that has no equal
items.example: Matchlessly is rare but keeps the -ly pattern.
items.exampleCN: matchlessly 少见，但符合 -ly 构词规律。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms matchlessness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 matchlessness。

items.example: The suffix -ful gives the opposite pattern to -less.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ful 与 -less 构成意义相反的构词对照。

items.example: Selfless shows -less removing self rather than a rival.
items.exampleCN: selfless 说明 -less 去掉的是「自我」而不是对手。
